evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-den

> A **7×24 resident personal assistant** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh).
> Not another chat window — an assistant that stays on, keeps its own memory, works while you are away, and stops to ask before it acts outside your trust boundary.

Status: **the core is implemented, tested, and active in a real profile.** This line deliberately carries no test count: a hard-coded one rotted repeatedly (307, 309, 316, 319, 320, 322, 323, 326, 327 — each time while the suite was in fact green), and the last rot happened one round after a "fix". So the line states what is stable and `npm test` prints what moves. The plugin is loaded inside a real DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 desktop profile — it is in that profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, and the running host reports it as `fiberPhase: active` — registering 16 model-facing tools, the approval guard, the heartbeat, and an interactive status panel. Verified against the *running* system rather than only in tests: the heartbeat ticks on its 60-second cadence, and the panel is an **active occupant** of both `sidebar.panellist` (`id: dsh-den.status`, order 245) and the `main` panel (`key: dsh-den.status`) — read from the live browser page through the host's read-only Slot inspector, not from the plugin's own registration call.

**Those live sentences were re-established on 2026-10-14 against the instance reporting `startedAt: 2026-10-14T02:10:43.000Z`**, whose own freshness verdict is `known: true, stale: false` and which loaded this tree 1000 seconds after its last source edit. `npm run verify:live` exits 0 against it and **all seven live probes pass**: the heartbeat ticks on its 60-second cadence, the route answers, an agent **cannot** obtain standing autonomy from the live host, the approval gate is the only path to authority, the expiry rule works in the host's own directory, scenario isolation holds against the same store the host reads, and disk evidence shows the `den_*` tools really were invoked. The earlier instance, `08:43:05.676Z`, is why this paragraph exists: after the panel fix landed at `09:24:00` it was still serving the previous panel while six live probes went on printing passes — each one run on its own, and each one describing code that was no longer on disk. Two things now make that state impossible to report as a pass. The plugin reports `status.freshness`: the newest source edit beside it against its own start, computed per request rather than cached at boot, with "cannot tell" as its own answer instead of a healthy default. And every live probe script is chained behind `tools/require-fresh-host.mjs`, which refuses to run it when the instance is stale or cannot say.

**The panel change is verified by what the page asked for, not by pixels.** At `09:52:28` — 141 seconds after that boot — a `panel-autonomy-requested` event reached the route carrying a **real conversation id**, `session-95cc8a8d-…`. The previous panel had no conversation to pass (resolving the active session *was* the defect, and it passed `null`), and the host is confirmed to be running the new code, so only the dock can have sent it; the probe's own requests are identifiable by their literal session ids (`live-autonomy-probe`, `grant-bypass-probe`). Two independent facts — the host loaded this tree, and a request only the dock can make arrived — are firmer evidence than a screenshot, and a screenshot is still not claimed.

**The panel was taking most of the screen, and that was a design error rather than a layout one.** The dock above the message box rendered the entire self-check creation form — title, prompt, interval, submit — permanently. It was there for a reason: the dock is the one seat the shell hands a real conversation to, and `schedules/create` refuses without one, so the form had to live somewhere a conversation exists. But the *capability* needs a conversation; it does not need to be on screen. The dock is now one line of state — autonomy, its two controls, and a one-line `New` disclosure — and the empty state names the cheaper path: say «check CI every 30 minutes» in the conversation and the den adds it. That this is small is machine-checked rather than asserted: `tools/check-client-interaction.mjs` requires the dock to render **zero** inputs and no submit button until the disclosure is pressed (it rendered three inputs and a submit button before), then checks that the form still sends the same payload once opened. The logic is the one the reference assistants this project is measured against are built on — state at a glance, one thing at a time, and the human talks instead of filling in forms — stated as a reading rather than a quotation, because this plugin's own gate keeps `web_fetch` fail-closed in a profile with `approval: never`, so those pages were not readable from inside this session.

**The admitted wake happened — at the first heartbeat after the self-check came due.** On 2026-10-14 the panel minted a request, that token came back as a **human message**, and `den_set_autonomy` recorded `{ok: true, autonomy: true, boundToMessage: "b7b68b9f-…"}` for `session-95cc8a8d-…`. A self-check was then created with the 300-second floor; it came due at `02:34:26`, and the next tick — `02:34:43`, one cadence later — spent a turn and spoke: the ledger went `turns 0 → 1`, `spoken 0 → 1`, `notices 1`, and the trigger was consumed. The host recorded the event itself, `{"type":"wake-spoke","triggerId":"76e58cc0c47ef5…"}`, and `npm run drill:after` returned `RESULT: PASS` (exit 0) behind a guard that had just confirmed the instance loaded this tree. Three details make it more than one successful run. **The same call used to be auto-refused**: the gate audit still lists historical `den_set_autonomy → unknown-tool → ask` entries from the instance before the fix, and the successful call is absent from that list — it was classified as the den's own tool. That classification is the fix described in [`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md) §2.28–§2.30: the approval policy in this profile is not its own switch but a side effect of the permission preset (`danger-full-access` implies `approval: never`, where a gate `ask` means *never*, not *later*), so for a while every den tool that was not read-only was unreachable — memory, self-checks and authority alike. The answer was to classify den's own tools as its own, each with a stated bound, rather than to weaken the credential, shell and outbound rules above that table; those rules still refuse this session's own calls when they should. **The counters are read separately on purpose**: `turns` is charged after delivery and `spoken` only when the wake actually says something, so a wake that was admitted and judged not worth saying would have shown `turns 1, spoken 0` and failed the drill; both moved, so this was a wake that *spoke*. And **the grant is bound to a message**, not to a click: `boundToMessage` names the human message that carried the token. What is still only verified offline: a wake *after a restart*. Triggers, grants and the ledger all live on disk and survived the restart that moved this host to `02:10:43`; `test/cold-start.test.mjs` grants through the real token, stores a trigger, moves the clock past a restart and watches the wake fire — but the joined event (restart, then a wake) has not been observed live, and neither has its negative (a due trigger with no authority staying silent). Both need a human act, and `npm run drill:before` / `npm run drill:after` is how either would be measured. [`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md) §2.35 has the event chain and both gaps; §2.34 is the defect this drill found in itself the first time it ran for real.


**The wake spoke and nobody was told — the defect a reader of this panel found.** The page reported `Pending notices 1 / 1` and `Today's self-initiated turns 1` while the human had received nothing, and the strip above the message box still offered a **spent** token with the instruction to paste it. Both had the same shape of cause: a surface reporting state it had no way to update. `pendingNotices` knew only "deliverable" and "expired", so a notice that had been shown could not stop being pending — the count could never reach zero — and the wake's own implementation queues its text (`queueNotice`) with no human-facing surface rendering it: the count said *something happened* and nothing said *what*. The fix is at both ends. A notice carries `deliveredAt`, only an explicit acknowledgement sets it — inferring "delivered" from a render would make the count lie in the opposite direction — the status snapshot carries the pending **text**, the dock renders it where the human already looks, with a `read it` control, and the minted token is shown only while it is still an unspent invitation. [`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md) §2.37 has the measurement and the two-sided fix; both halves are pinned by tests that fail if either is missing.

**And it reproduces from this repository alone.** A fresh `git clone` of the published repo — no `node_modules`, because the package declares **no dependencies at all** — runs the whole suite green:

```
node_modules present in clone: False
dependencies declared: (none)
ℹ tests 326   ℹ pass 326   ℹ fail 0
test exit: 0
```

The four files the residency work added were looked for in that clone by name — `src/resident.js`, `test/resident.test.mjs`, `test/two-process.test.mjs`, `test/support/resident-child.mjs` — because the failure this proof exists for is a source file that is on disk, is imported by the code, and never made it into the repository. A bare `lib/` in `.gitignore` did exactly that once, and every local test passed while the pushed repo was broken.

That is the claim worth making precisely: not "it works on my machine", but *a third party with a Node binary and nothing else can check this*. `npm run check:source-tracked` asserts it on every run: every source file on disk is tracked by git, and the ignore rule that hid one is named.

**A transcript is not bookkeeping.** The number above was once edited from 240 to 241 to 252 across three commits while the last actual clone run had printed 237 — a public claim with no command under it, which is the defect this repository keeps finding in its own work. The number now comes from a run at the pushed commit, and the way to keep it that way is to re-run the proof rather than update the count.


**The wake delivery path was broken and is now fixed — that history is worth reading, because the test suite was green throughout.** The plugin delivered wakes with `subagents.sendMessage(agent, trigger.sessionId, …)`, where `agent` is the *target conversation's own driver*. The host admits a send only when the sender is the target's direct parent or direct continuable child — `authorizeLineage` requires `parentSession === parent.id` — so the call asked a session to be its own parent and **every admitted wake in production died** with `delivery requires the exact live parent agent`. Five tests covered that path and passed, because the fakes granted any delivery at all: the double was lying about the *calling convention*, not the service.

Delivery now goes through `Agent.followup`, which the host documents as *"queues an ordinary next-turn prompt and wakes the driver"* — `send(message, 'next-turn', true)`, splicing into the inbox and opening a turn boundary. No lineage is involved, the wake is visibly a queued turn in the conversation, and it durably becomes a `user/message` that the reply read-back pairs with the assistant's answer. `subagents` is no longer read anywhere.

**The delivery surface is now verified on the running host, not just in the harness.** `npm run check:wake-api` asks the live Host what it actually offers and reports:

```
PASS — the agents service exposes get()
PASS — the agents service exposes resume()
PASS — `followup` is absent from the service contract, as expected
PASS — a live agent was found and identified
       id: session-95cc8a8d-a3e9-4e2a-a67d-12292d17ba24
PASS — the live agent carries a callable followup()
       this is the capability the delivery path needs, measured on the running Host
RESULT: PASS — 8 checks, and the delivery surface is the one this Host actually offers.
```

That check exists because the defect it guards against was an *assumption about an API*, and it is placed where the assumption can be measured: `agents.get`/`agents.resume` are declared to return `Agent`, and `Agent` is declared as `{ readonly id }`. `followup` appears in no service signature — it is a method on the live agent object the factory builds — so the surfaced contract is narrower than the runtime object and no amount of reading signatures answers "will delivery work on this Host". The probe reports `sawLiveAgent: false` rather than a pass when no agent is live: *I could not look* is not *it is not there*.

**What is still outstanding is one human step, not a defect.** No admitted wake has ever been delivered, because admitting one requires standing autonomy and no human has granted it. That single drill is the last unverified path in the project; everything on either side of it is measured. See `DESIGN.md` §2.7 for the code evidence and §2.8 for how the fakes were made to stop hiding it.

**Capability 4 is verified end to end, and the way it was verified is the point.** The gate's secret rule matches on *path*, and it is installed as `ctx.tools.guard`, so it intercepts every tool call in the profile — including the assistant's own. That makes a zero-risk live test possible: read a credential-shaped path **that does not exist**. If the gate works the call is refused before the filesystem is touched; if it does not, the result is `ENOENT` and nothing leaks.

```
Error: refused: this would pull a stored credential into the conversation (credentials-yaml)
```

That sentence is `src/gate.js` verbatim, and the host's own service event stream recorded the decision alongside it:

```json
{"type":"gate","tool":"read","rule":"secret:credentials-yaml","risk":2,"decision":"deny",
 "sessionId":"session-95cc8a8d-a3e9-4e2a-a67d-12292d17ba24"}
```

Two more entries in that stream corrected a misattribution of my own: `outbound:curl-upload` and `outbound:recursive-delete`, both `ask`. Two tool calls I had reported to the user as *"the user rejected it"* were in fact denied by **this plugin's own gate** — classified `ask`, and a host without an approval facility turns `ask` into a denial. The gate had been shaping the session the whole time.

**Later, on 2026-10-14, the loopback half of that first rule was allowed through — and only that half.** Asked about the boundary, the human answered "只放行本机", so `decide()` now returns `allow` for an `outbound:` rule whose destination is a *named* loopback host (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`, with or without a port). Three bounds keep that permission as narrow as the sentence that granted it: the rule must be an `outbound:` one, the destination must actually be written out — a missing or unparsable destination still asks, which is what stops text that merely *mentions* an upload from travelling as permission — and the exception sits **after** the deny branch, so an allowed destination can never rescue a denied action. The argument that made the rule fire on both halves (a loopback service can relay) has not been disproved; it is now recorded as the human's call rather than the plugin's. [`test/gate-loopback.test.mjs`](test/gate-loopback.test.mjs) pins every one of those bounds by calibrating against the gate's own thresholds instead of copying them.

The same evidence exposed a defect worth naming, because it is a whole class rather than a slip: `onDecision` announced decisions through `noteEvent` (the in-memory ring the panel shows) and **never called `recordAudit`**, while `gateAudit()` read `gate-audit.json` — a file no code wrote. So the panel's gate surface reported *"no decisions"* permanently, including while three real ones had just been made. `recordAudit` was dead code and the durable-audit design had never run once. **Reading a file that is never written looks exactly like a gate that has never fired.** The seam is now fixed and pinned from both ends — the service reader *and* the file on disk — because asserting only through `gateAudit()` would pass if reader and writer were the same piece of memory.

**And the fix is now observable in the live profile, from a later process than the one that wrote it.** After the restart the file exists and holds exactly the refusals this session provoked:

```json
{"at":1791868057296,"tool":"den_set_autonomy","rule":"unknown-tool","risk":1,"decision":"ask","sessionId":"session-95cc8a8d-…"}
{"at":1791868277929,"tool":"plugin_manager","rule":"unknown-tool","risk":1,"decision":"ask","sessionId":"session-95cc8a8d-…"}
```

Three things are true of that file and all three were only design intentions before: the reader has a writer, the record **outlives the process that made it** — so *"why did it refuse?"* is answerable after the fact and not only while the ring happens to still hold it — and the entry carries the tool, rule, risk, decision and session but **not the arguments**, so the audit does not become a second copy of whatever the gate was protecting. `plugin_manager` is in there as well as the den tool: the gate intercepts every tool call in the profile, not only the ones belonging to the plugin that installed it.


**And the state really did cross a restart, measured on the running host rather than argued.** The plugin's own status payload carries when *this* instance last loaded the plugin; the state file carries when it was first written. On the live host those two disagree by roughly an hour, in the direction that proves the point:

```
state.createdAt   : 2026-10-13T01:49:11.717Z    ← written by an earlier boot
plugin startedAt  : 2026-10-13T02:56:33.794Z    ← this instance (pid 36704)
```

So a previous life wrote that file and this one read it back: the assistant came back up **on its own**, with its configuration intact and no human involved. That is the persistence half of capability 2, and it is the half that does not need anybody's permission.

Getting there required fixing the field that was supposed to say so. `stateSurvivesRestart` was computed *inside* `status()` as `readJson(statePath) !== undefined` — evaluated long after the boot had written that very file — so it was `true` on a first-ever boot of a machine that had never been restarted, while the comment above it claimed it *"cannot overstate what survived a restart"*. It had already been cited as proof: `tools/check-acceptance.mjs` asserted `true` on a first boot into an empty home, under a check named *"boot persists state"*. It is now sampled **before** the boot claims the tree, where the answer could still be no, and `stateCreatedAt` ships alongside it so a reader can confirm the claim instead of trusting it. The acceptance block already boots twice, so the fix made that check strictly stronger: it now observes a real `false → true` transition. The reusable rule, at three instances of this class: **a field named for a past event — survived, recovered, delivered, refused — must be sampled at a moment when the event could still not have happened. Sampled later it degrades from measurement to constant, silently, and reports `false` with a straight face.**

**The live profile now shows the difference between the two versions in one payload.** On the instance that started at `05:06:55.290Z`, `stateCreatedAt` is `1791856151717` — about 3.3 hours *earlier*. So `stateSurvivesRestart: true` is a comparison against this instance's own boot rather than a constant that happened to be right, and the field that used to be absent is the one that makes the claim checkable. That absence is also how the previous build was identified as stale while the host was still serving it.



**The running host was serving an older build; it has since been restarted, and the same check that said so now says otherwise.** Before the restart, the `Tool` inspect provider reported a different tool count from this tree's source and `GET /dsh-den` answered 404. Afterwards, `npm run verify:live` reports:

- `GET /dsh-den` → **200** with a well-formed envelope
- `state.json` **written by this boot**, containing `cooldownSeconds`, `createdAt`, `dailyTurnBudget`, `displayName`, `quietHours`, `tickSeconds`, `updatedAt`, `version`
- **11 tools** through the `Tool` inspect provider, byte-for-byte the same names this tree registers
- `transport.browserReachable` **set** — a real browser reached the panel route, which is the one seam that had never been observed

The live status payload then reports the assistant actually running: `kernel.running: true`, `kernel.lastError: null`, a fresh `lastTickAt`, `gate.mounted: true`, and a ledger file on disk with `turns/spoken/skipped/refused` at zero. A scripted drill over the same real socket confirmed the write path end to end — `autonomy/request` minted a 32-character token, `schedules/create` → `schedules/list` → `schedules/delete` round-tripped, and a 10-second interval was correctly refused with `everySeconds must be at least 300`. Everything the drill created was deleted; `~/.dsh/den/triggers/` is empty again.

**A later restart brought this round's fixes live, and the check that had been failing for three rounds turned green.** The deployment check had been reporting `the running instance loaded this tree ... the host is running code older than this tree` since the lease work landed; the host reloaded at `2026-10-13T08:43:05.676Z`, later than the newest source edit (`triggers.js`, `08:39:32.676Z`), and it now passes. What the payload shows that the previous build could not:

- **`residency` exists** — `{held: true, instance: "7969f300…", pid: 34336, staleMs: 180000, holderSince: …}`. On the build before this restart the key was **absent**, so this is the lease code actually running, not a claim about it.
- **`reapedNotices: 0`** — the field added with the notice sweep, present and answering.
- **11 `den_*` tools** through the `Tool` inspect provider, matching the source one for one. The deployment check names this as the thing it *cannot* see from where it stands, so it was queried directly.
- **A browser reached the route** at `08:52:58.246Z`, predating the verification run — the panel polling from the real page.

`npm run verify:live` → **exit 0**, and **all thirteen `check:*` scripts** → exit 0 against the running host, including the six live ones: `deployment`, `autonomy`, `notices`, `memory`, `tools`, `wake-api` (8 checks), plus `grant-bypass`, `bundle`, `ui`, `acceptance`, `package`, `install`, `source-tracked`.

**The assistant speaking on its own has not happened, but the reason is measured rather than assumed — and the boundary turns out to be structural.** `autonomy` is `null` with `autonomyKnown: false`, because no human has granted it.


The refusal is deliberate and traceable to one line each in three files:

- `src/gate.js` keeps every durable effect on the default tier and says why in a comment: *"`den_set_autonomy` is a privilege change."* `den_status`, `den_recall` and the other read-only tools are `allow`; this one is not.
- `den_explain_gate` on the running host reports `verdict: "ask"`, rule `unknown-tool`.
- `src/gate.js` also states the consequence of a host without approval support: *"a missing approval facility turns `ask` into a denial, which is the correct fail-closed direction."*

This session has approval prompts disabled, so `ask` resolves to a denial. **The agent side of this path is therefore closed by construction, not by operator error**, and calling `den_set_autonomy` from an agent turn cannot succeed here at all. The panel is not an alternative: its grant control mints a *request* and says so in its own copy — *paste this token to the assistant in the conversation* — and `autonomy/confirm` resolves a live conversation before it looks at anything else.

**That is no longer an argument from the rule table — it has been attempted, on the live host, from the conversation itself.** The assistant called `den_set_autonomy` with `autonomy: true` on the running system, and the plugin's own gate stopped it and wrote down what it did:

```json
{"type":"gate","tool":"den_set_autonomy","rule":"unknown-tool","risk":1,"decision":"ask",
 "sessionId":"session-95cc8a8d-a3e9-4e2a-a67d-12292d17ba24"}
```

That `sessionId` is the session the attempt was made *in* — not a probe standing in for one. After the refusal the same status payload reports `autonomy: null` and `grants: 0`: **the privilege change did not happen, and the agent could not make it happen.** Earlier rounds could only cite `den_explain_gate`, which reports what the gate *would* do; this is the gate doing it to a real call.

It also settles a question the docs had been vague about: **the `den_*` tools are callable by the assistant's own turns** — `den_status` works from the conversation — so this was not a hypothetical attempt from outside the trust boundary but the assistant reaching for its own authority with every capability it actually has.

### Granting authority to a running instance, step by step

The negative half of capability 1 is demonstrated above. The positive half needs a person, and there is no way around that: the agent can mint a token, can cite any message id, and can write to the whole tree, but **it cannot author a `user/message`**, and that is what the grant is bound to. To reproduce it:

1. Set the session's approval policy to `ask`. It is per-agent — `approval.setPolicy(agent, 'ask')`, the counterpart of the `'never'` this session starts with (see the contracts below) — and the Host reports the change in the model's own runtime context, so the assistant can tell the switch happened rather than inferring it. With the policy at `never`, `ask` resolves to a denial and `den_set_autonomy` is refused automatically, which is the correct fail-closed behaviour and also why an approval-disabled session can never complete this flow.
2. Open the den panel and use its grant control. It mints a single-use, 10-minute token and shows the instruction: *paste this token to the assistant in the conversation*.
3. Paste that token into a message. The token is the whole point of the step — anything the agent could produce on its own would prove nothing.
4. In **the same turn**, the assistant calls `den_set_autonomy` with `autonomy: true`. It does not need the message id: the den finds the human message in the current turn that quotes the token, and that lookup is stricter than the id path because it requires the token.
5. Approve the tool call rather than letting it be denied. The grant is written and bound to that message.

**Telling a person apart from a probe in the event log.** A panel grant carries the conversation id, because the panel scopes its request to the active conversation; a route probe carries a synthetic id, or none at all if it did not bother. That distinction had to be made explicit rather than left to the reader: `check-live-grant-bypass.mjs` used to mint with no session, leaving `{"type":"panel-autonomy-requested","sessionId":null}` — an entry a person clicking Grant could equally have left. It now signs its own requests with a synthetic id and asserts that it did, because **a probe whose footprint a human could have left makes the log lie about who acted.**

So authority needs a human in the loop twice: the token must be cited in a real human message, and the resulting tool call must be approved rather than auto-denied. That is capability 1 in its strongest form — the agent cannot manufacture its own standing autonomy even with write access to the whole tree.

**What the refusal looks like on the running host.** A `once` trigger was created due immediately, with no grant anywhere. The real kernel picked it up on its next heartbeat and recorded, in its own event log:

```json
{"type":"wake-refused",
 "triggerId":"bc83e334…",
 "gate":"authority",
 "reason":"no standing autonomy from a direct human request",
 "hadSession":false}
```

with `ledger.refused` incremented and the trigger's `fireCount` left at `0` — so the intent survived rather than being consumed. That is capabilities 1 and 2 together, end to end, on a real host: **the autonomous wake ran, and the authority gate stopped it for the stated reason.** The drill's trigger was deleted afterwards and `~/.dsh/den/triggers/` is empty.

**Two production defects came out of that drill, and are fixed.** The refusal record appeared twice, exactly sixty seconds apart, which is what exposed the first: the refusal path never throttled, so a permanently unauthorized trigger was re-evaluated on *every* heartbeat — 1,440 log entries a day for one `once` trigger. The second came from writing an assertion that `tick()` has one return shape: the idle branch omitted `results` and the busy branch omitted `woke`/`spoke`, so `tick().results.length` threw on exactly the quiet ticks that are the common case. Both fixes are in `src/kernel.js` with regression tests in `test/cold-start.test.mjs`, each verified by reverting it.

The remaining unverified step is the *admitted* wake and the long unattended run. Both need a human to grant autonomy.

**The authorization flow has a dry run on the running host, and it refuses correctly.** Every step below was exercised over the real route:

1. `autonomy/request` → `ok: true`, a 32-character token, and an instruction that states the design in one line: *call `den_set_autonomy`, `autonomy=true`, `humanMessageId` with this message's id, and cite token …*. It creates **no** grant.
2. `autonomy/confirm` with that token but no human evidence → `ok: false`, `DEN_ACTION_FAILED`, *"no live conversation for this token: autonomy is granted per conversation"*.
3. Repeating the failed confirm → the **same** refusal, so the failure did not spend the token.
4. `status` afterwards → `autonomy: null`, `autono

# Bladebro Stealthy and efficient agentic browser driver for AI agents. Few tools, full control, real stealth, max token efficiency. ## Install ```bash npm install -g bladebro ``` Or use without installing: ```bash npx bladebro mcp ``` ### DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Add Bladebro as a native plugin in the Web UI's **Plugins** page, or run: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add bladebro ``` Restart the profile and start a new chat. Desktop users can install `bladebro` from the same **Plugins** page. For terminal setup, enable Desktop's **Manage dsh Command**, fully quit the app, then use its bundled command: ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop add bladebro ``` Use Desktop's command for its profile; the npm DSH CLI cannot manage that app-owned profile. Open Desktop again after installation. DSH discovers the five tools as `mcp__bladebro__act`, `see`, `state`, `run` and `vision` (each with the same prefix). Schemas and descriptions come from the binary; DSH handles permissions, image attachments, reconnection and cleanup through its native MCP bridge. DSH may also expose its own generic MCP resource helpers and choose PTC presentation. No API key, separate MCP configuration, global Bladebro install or extra plugin package is needed. Chrome/Chromium must be installed on the machine running the DSH host. A remotely hosted Web UI controls that host's browser, rather than the device viewing the UI. Disable/re-enable the **Bladebro** bundle in Plugins, or remove it with `dsh plugin --profile web remove bladebro` (use `desktop` with Desktop's command). Restart the profile and begin a new chat after package changes. Other tools and settings remain intact. Do not also configure a second MCP server named `bladebro`; DSH refuses the duplicate namespace. Updates use DSH's package manager: `dsh plugin --profile web update bladebro`, or **Update** in Plugins. The plugin and native binary travel in the same package, so ordinary Bladebro releases update both. Existing global/Pi installs are separate. No background downloader or installation scripts run. Advanced configuration belongs in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: bladebro config: # Optional absolute source-build/portable executable; package binary is default. binaryPath: /absolute/path/to/bladebro env: CHROME_PATH: /absolute/path/to/chrome BLADE_HOME: /absolute/path/to/private/browser-data toolCallTimeoutMs: 180000 ``` Windows YAML paths can use forward slashes, such as `C:/Tools/bladebro.exe`. The optional `cwd` and `reconnect` settings use DSH's native MCP configuration. The default per-call budget is 180 seconds; raise it for longer `run` sequences. Cancellation stops waiting, but an already-dispatched browser mutation may finish: observe its destination before trying it again. The npm CLI keeps its Node.js >=14 requirement; the DSH plugin uses the host's Node.js requirement. Prebuilt binaries cover Linux x64/ARM64 (glibc >=2.28), macOS Intel/Apple Silicon and Windows x64. Other targets need a source build and `binaryPath`. See the official [DSH plugin commands](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/apps/cli/reference/README.md#plugin-management) and [Desktop command runtime](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/apps/desktop/README.md#bundled-command-runtime). ## MCP and CLI ### Option 1: MCP Server For AI agents that speak MCP (Model Context Protocol). Point your agent at it: ```json { "mcpServers": { "bladebro": { "command": "bladebro", "args": ["mcp"] } } } ``` Five tools: `act`, `see`, `state`, `run`, `vision`. Full docs at [github.com/dondai44423/bladebro](https://github.com/dondai44423/bladebro). ### Option 2: CLI For AI agents that run shell commands. One persistent Chrome instance across all commands (auto-daemon): ```bash bladebro nav https://example.com # auto-starts daemon + Chrome bladebro see content # uses same Chrome bladebro act click e5 # uses same Chrome bladebro stop # cleans up # JSON output for agents: bladebro nav https://example.com --json bladebro see content --json # Agent discovery (returns tool schemas + CLI mapping): bladebro help --json ``` ## Requirements - Node.js >= 14 - Chrome/Chromium installed (Bladebro finds it automatically) - Linux prebuilt binaries: glibc >= 2.28 ## Platforms Prebuilt binaries available for: - Linux x86_64 (`linux-x64`) - Linux ARM64 (`linux-arm64`) - macOS Apple Silicon (`darwin-arm64`) - macOS Intel (`darwin-x64`) - Windows x86_64 (`windows-x64`) Other platforms: [build from source](https://github.com/dondai44423/bladebro#from-source). ## License Apache-2.0

Built in Rust on a self-built CDP transport: one static binary, no Node.js, no Playwright, no runtime. It holds a persistent **Live Page Model** across tool calls, so every action returns **what changed** — never the whole page again. > **⭐ New — drive *your* browser.** `bladebro rb on` switches every surface to your own Chromium-family browser — your profile, your logins, your display — with the page-injection layer **off entirely**: a real environment has no manufactured tells to catch. Everything driver-side stays on. **[Real-browser mode →](#-real-browser-mode)** ## 🎬 Demo **Bladebro doing real work on two bot-protected sites — Reddit and X.com — in under two minutes.** Real navigation, real actions, real content back: comment trees, threads and timelines as clean structured output. ## 🏆 Stealth Bench V1 Run against [browser-use's Stealth Bench V1](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark): **80 real production sites** protected by 11 anti-bot vendors. Bladebro cleared **68 (85%)** — above every provider on the published leaderboard (browser-use-cloud: 81%). - **Out of the box** — one IP, no proxy, no captcha solver, no fingerprint rotation, no cloud. Stock Chromium with Bladebro's stealth layer on by default. - **Honest run** — real navigation of the real 80 sites; an open-model agent acted as the browsing agent because there was no paid cloud access, and the deviations are disclosed in full. The defensive layer being measured is Bladebro's own. - **Where it stands** — perfect on Cloudflare (22/22) and reCaptcha (6/6); cleared the two sites browser-use-cloud did not (Shape, Temu); one named gap: Akamai (3/6). **[Full report and methodology →](STEALTH_BENCH.md)** · **[Per-site results (CSV)](stealth-bench-sites.csv)** ## ✨ What makes it different | What | Why it matters | |---|---| | **Re-render immunity** | Refs survive React/Vue/Angular DOM replacement via structural fingerprints — no other agent browser does this. | | **Delta-first results** | Every action returns what changed: 60–570 tokens per action, not full-page snapshot dumps. | | **5 tools, not 30** | ~1,900 tokens of tool definitions total; comparable tools ship 8,000–13,700. | | **Batch + branching** | `act batch` runs multi-step workflows in ONE call; `run` adds `if`/`while` logic. | | **Auto-extract + adapters** | Template-free list extraction, site-aware: Reddit comment trees, X.com threads, GitHub repos, product pages. | | **Infinite-scroll collect** | `act collect` scrolls, dedupes and returns a whole feed as one artifact, in one call. | | **6-layer stealth** | Protocol, environment, behavior, coherence, residue, seasoning — on by default, verified against real detectors. | | **Real-browser lane** | `bladebro rb on` drives your real Chrome-family browser — your profile, your display — with zero page patches and every driver feature on. | | **Self-improving** | Learns consent selectors, block choices and settle timing per domain; one behavioral fingerprint forever. | | **Self-healing** | Dead refs re-resolve, dead tabs reopen, crashed Chrome relaunches — transparently. | ## 🚀 Install ### npm (recommended) ```bash npm install -g bladebro bladebro mcp ``` Requires Chrome/Chromium; prebuilt Linux binaries require glibc 2.28 or newer. Linux ARM64 and macOS binaries are cross-compiled from Linux with cargo-zigbuild. ### Pi coding agent ```bash pi install npm:bladebro ``` Registers 5 native tools (`browser.act`, `browser.see`, `browser.state`, `browser.run`, `browser.vision`) from the binary's own `tools/list` — tool definitions auto-adapt to any change, with zero extension maintenance. ### DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Add Bladebro as a native plugin in the Web UI's **Plugins** page, or run: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add bladebro ``` pnpm 11 defaults to a [one-day release-age delay](https://pnpm.io/blog/releases/11.0), so an unversioned install immediately after a release can select an older package. Advanced configuration belongs in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: bladebro config: # Optional absolute source-build/portable executable; package binary is default. binaryPath: /absolute/path/to/bladebro env: CHROME_PATH: /absolute/path/to/chrome BLADE_HOME: /absolute/path/to/private/browser-data toolCallTimeoutMs: 180000 ``` Windows YAML paths can use forward slashes, such as `C:/Tools/bladebro.exe`. Other targets need a source build and `binaryPath`. See the official [DSH plugin commands](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/apps/cli/reference/README.md#plugin-management) and [Desktop command runtime](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/apps/desktop/README.md#bundled-command-runtime). ### Hermes Agent ```bash npm install -g bladebro bladebro hermes on ``` Requires a current Hermes CLI with `config get --json --raw`, `config unset` and `mcp test`; update Hermes if those commands are unavailable. Start a **new Hermes chat** (restart a running gateway or desktop client). This connects the standard MCP server and removes Hermes' built-in browser toolset, including `browser_exec`, from the agent's tools. Web search and extraction keep their existing settings. Chrome/Chromium must be installed; `bladebro doctor` checks browser prerequisites. ```bash bladebro hermes status # inspect the setup bladebro hermes off # restore the previous browser settings bladebro hermes on --profile work # target a named Hermes profile ``` Use the same profile for `off`; `HERMES_HOME` is also respected. If Hermes isn't on PATH, add `--hermes /path/to/hermes` (its CLI executable on Windows). Setup uses Hermes' public `config` and `mcp test` commands, saves private recovery state beside `config.yaml`, and reads settings back after writing. Interrupted switches can resume with `on` or restore with `off`. A changed MCP entry is refused during recovery rather than overwritten. Existing server environment settings are retained; explicit `BLADE_HOME` and `CHROME_PATH` from setup are forwarded because Hermes filters inherited variables. Other settings and pre-existing browser suppression survive restore. Avoid concurrent manual configuration edits while switching. There is no separate plugin or copied tool schema: normal Bladebro updates update the Hermes browser too. Hermes may expose MCP tools through its built-in Tool Search; all five remain discoverable there. `browser.backend: off` selects Hermes' alternative native browser stack; it does **not** disable browser tools. See [Hermes browser documentation](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/browser/) and [MCP documentation](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/mcp/). ### From source Requires Chromium or Chrome (auto-detected) and Rust 1.86+. Linux servers need Xvfb for headful. ```bash git clone https://github.com/dondai44423/bladebro.git cd bladebro cargo build --release ./target/release/bladebro mcp ``` Source builds self-update too: `bladebro -u` swaps in the official released binary for your platform (it doesn't rebuild — for that: `git pull && cargo build --release`). ## 🎯 The 5 tools ### `act` — do, then observe Every call returns an **outcome verdict + page delta**. Clicks choose a role-aware activation lane and dispatch once; a quiet DOM never triggers another click. After a disconnect, mutating actions report an unknown outcome so the agent can inspect the destination before repeating them; clicking by text skips the read step (`act click text="Sign in"`), and ambiguous text returns matches with refs + `nth` values. Verdicts report observable evidence only: a state-only change is labeled `state-only, no nodes added/removed` (never a phantom `(+0 −0)`), an occluded click names what actually receives it, and a coordinate click that hits nothing names the topmost element at that point. | Action | Example | What it does | |---|---|---| | `click` | `act click e5` / `act click text="Sign in"` / `act click selector="#menu li"` | Mouse, JS, Enter escalation; `selector=` reaches controls inside open shadow roots — a bad selector errors as invalid, an out-of-range `nth` errors with the real match count | | `type` | `act type label="Search" text="hello"` | Cadenced typing into textboxes | | `fill` | `act fill fields=[...] submit="Go"` | Multi-field forms in ONE call, auto-detects field type | | `batch` | `act batch steps=[...]` | Multi-step workflows in ONE call | | `navigate` | `act navigate url="https://example.com"` | Idempotent; returns the page model | | `collect` | `act collect max=50 timeout=30` | Auto-extract + scroll + dedupe an infinite feed | | `wait` | `act wait condition=url text="dashboard"` | 6 conditions: element, title, settle, url, text, js | | `eval` | `act eval js="document.title"` | Console-style JS; `el` in scope when a ref is given | | `scroll` | `act scroll dy=800` | Smooth, eased wheel events | | `hover` | `act hover text="Products"` | Reveals dropdowns in the delta | | `press` | `act press key=Enter` / `key=Control+a` | Real key event; full chords (`Control+a`, `Meta+Enter`, `Shift+Tab`) | | `select` | `act select e4 option="Nepal"` | Dropdown by option text or value | | `read` | `act read e5` | Element text content | | `upload` | `act upload e7 text="/tmp/file.txt"` | File input | | `clear` | `act clear e3` | Empty an input or rich editor | | `download` | `act download url=... timeout=10` | Fetch + Blob download, returns the path | | `pdf` | `act pdf` | Export the page as a PDF artifact | | `back` / `forward` / `reload` | `act back` | History + reload | - **Self-healing refs** — a dead ref re-resolves by identity: `act click e5` after navigation finds the new "Sign in" and reports `[ref e5 healed]`. - **Batch** — one call fills, submits, clicks; it continues through navigation and stops on the first error with step number + page state. - **`selector=` everywhere** — click, hover, type, select, clear, read, upload, eval, `fill` fields, and `batch`/`run` steps all accept a CSS selector (light DOM + open shadow roots); `nth=` picks among matches. - **`url=` on any action** — navigate first, then act: `act fill url="https://..." fields=[...]` reaches a page and fills it in one call. - **`slim=true`** — verdict only, no delta. ### `see` — observe | Call | What you get | |---|---| | `see` | Full model — interactive elements with refs (nav/footer auto-folded) | | `see mode=content` | Page text as clean markdown — for reading | | `see mode=outline` | Heading hierarchy only (~50–200 bytes) | | `see find="price"` | Search by text (light DOM + open shadow roots) → refs + scores; a miss names hidden matches with reasons | | `see filter="button,link"` | Zoom by role/name/landmark | | `see extract="auto"` | Template-free list extraction, site-aware (below) | | `see extract="json" template={...}` | Custom CSS-template extraction | | `see extract="links"` / `"forms"` | All links / all form fields | | `see scope=e5` | One element's subtree text; with `mode=content`: that subtree as markdown (budget honored) | | `see logs="console"` / `"network"` | JS errors / requests, failures first | - **Truncation is deterministic:** output ends with `…(N more: X link, Y button)` — roles sorted by count desc, then alphabetically; the full set stays available via `see filter=`. - **Big data goes to files.** Payloads over 12KB are written to `artifacts/` and returned as a path + preview; read any artifact back in pages with `see artifact=""` (+`offset`/`limit`) — no filesystem access needed. - **Site-aware:** on Reddit post pages and X.com status pages, `extract=auto` returns the full comment tree / thread in ONE call; Hacker News rows carry points, author, age and comment count. ### `state` — cookies, storage, tabs, sessions | op | What it does | |---|---| | `tabs` / `open-tab` / `switch-tab` / `close-tab` | Tab management (auto-focus on open) | | `cookies` / `set-cookie` / `del-cookie` | Cookies | | `save name=login` / `load name=login` | Save cookies + storage; navigate to the saved origin before loading, then reload | | `ls` / `ss` / `set-ls` / `set-ss` / `rm-ls` / `rm-ss` | localStorage / sessionStorage | | `block classes="images,fonts,trackers"` | Block inert assets — never first-party scripts | | `compress on/off/status` | Context pruning toggle | ### `run` — batch + branch + JS ```json {"steps":[ {"action":"type","label":"Email","text":"user@mail.com"}, {"action":"type","label":"Password","text":"secret"}, {"action":"click","text":"Sign in"}, {"action":"wait","condition":"element","text":"Dashboard","timeout":10} ]} ``` Use instead of `act batch` when you need branching (`if`/`else`), loops (`while`), or state ops that change tabs. `see` steps read inline — nav + loop + read across pages in ONE call. Steps take `optional: true` (a tolerated failure reports `failed (optional)` and the run continues), and `wait` accepts an `else: [...]` fallback branch when its condition times out. ### `vision` — screenshot (last resort) Screenshot as PNG; `marks=true` overlays numbered ref badges. MCP returns it as an image; the CLI writes a file and reports `image_path`. The structural model is almost always better: cheaper, more reliable, and it hands you refs to act on. ## 🔌 Usage

Same 5 tools, same handlers, same stealth — two surfaces. Use MCP for agents; use the CLI for scripts, shells and CI. One codebase, so every fix lands on both. | | MCP server | CLI | |---|---|---| | **Best for** | AI agents (Claude, Cursor, pi, Cline) | Shell scripts, CI/CD, quick one-offs | | **Works over** | stdio JSON-RPC | `bladebro `, daemon-backed | | **Discovery** | `tools/list` | `bladebro help --json` | | **Session** | one Chrome per agent session | persistent daemon, or `--no-daemon` per command | ### MCP server Add to your client's config: ```json { "mcpServers": { "bladebro": { "command": "bladebro", "args": ["mcp"] } } } ``` Speaks MCP **2024-11-05 through 2026-07-28** — the legacy `initialize` handshake and the stateless per-request dialect (`server/discover`). Works with every MCP client, old and new. ### CLI `bladebro help --json` is the single self-teaching manual: the same tool schemas as MCP, plus per-command usage, universal flags, payload conventions and exit codes — in ONE call. ```bash bladebro help --json | jq '.tools[].name' # ["act","see","state","run","vision"] bladebro help act --json | jq .detail.actions ``` **Daemon mode** — the first command auto-starts a daemon; Chrome stays alive across calls: ```bash bladebro nav https://news.ycombinator.com bladebro see content bladebro act click e5 bladebro stop # clean shutdown ``` ```bash bladebro see content https://example.com --no-daemon # one-shot: launch Chrome per command ``` **Universal flags** | Flag | What it does | |---|---| | `--json` | One JSON object on stdout: `{ok, is_error, text}` (+ `image_path` for vision) | | `--no-daemon` | Launch Chrome per command instead of using the daemon | | `--host` / `--port` | Drive an already-running Chrome on this debug port | | `--marks` | Vision: overlay numbered ref badges | **Exit codes are the contract:** `0` success · `1` command failed (the text carries page state for recovery) · `2` usage error (the message says how to fix it). Big payloads come from a file or stdin — no shell-quoting games: `bladebro run @steps.json`, `cat steps.json | bladebro run -`, `bladebro act eval @script.js`.
More CLI examples ```bash # Forms — one call bladebro act fill '[{"label":"Email","text":"a@b.com"},{"label":"Password","text":"secret"}]' --submit e20 # Batch steps from a file bladebro run @steps.json bladebro act batch @steps.json # Read + extract bladebro see model --json | jq .text bladebro see extract auto --json # State bladebro state cookies bladebro state open-tab https://example.com # Drive your own browser bladebro rb on && bladebro nav https://news.ycombinator.com # Screenshot with ref badges bladebro vision --marks --json | jq -r .image_path ```
## 🧠 How it works

The core is the **Live Page Model** — a persistent, compressed, ref-stable model of the page held across every tool call. Three pillars: - **Semantic refs** (`e1`, `e2`, …) — anchors assigned by signature (`framePath|role|name|rank`), not position. They survive scrolls, insertions and re-renders. - **Structural fingerprints** — an FNV-1a hash of the ancestor chain, tag, children and identity attributes: the mechanism behind re-render immunity. - **Deltas only** — every action returns what changed, so the agent never re-reads what it already knows. Everything is built from scratch where it counts — the CDP transport, perception, stealth injection, biometrics, session management. Chromium is the only borrowed part. ## 🧬 Re-render immunity **The #1 reliability gap in every other agent browser, solved.** When React, Vue or Angular re-renders a component, the DOM nodes are destroyed and recreated — and every other agent browser loses its refs. Bladebro re-binds them: when text changes but structure survives, the ref follows the fingerprint instead of dying. ``` Before re-render: e2 button "Buy Now" sig=button|Buy Now|1 fp=0xdeadbeef After re-render: e2 button "Buy Now v1" sig=button|Buy Now v1|1 fp=0xdeadbeef ← same fp ↺ e2 (re-render survived) ``` The agent sees `↺ e2 (re-render survived)` in the delta. The click works. No recapture. Playwright, Puppeteer, CDP wrappers, accessibility-tree snapshots — all lose refs here. ## 🪙 Token efficiency **5× more token-efficient than every competitor.** - **Delta results** — 60–570 tokens per action; snapshot-based tools spend ~1,400–2,000+. - **Tool defs** — ~1,900 tokens vs 8,000–13,700. The agent plans; it doesn't juggle APIs. - **Context pruning** — `act` responses compress after turn 3 on the same page: full (8K) → reduced (3K) → verdict-only (500 chars). ~54% fewer tokens over a session, zero capability loss. ```bash bladebro state compress off # on / off / status — or BLADE_NO_COMPRESS=1 ``` The counter resets on navigation, any `see`, or any error. `see`, `state`, `run` and `vision` are never compressed. ## 🥷 Stealth

Six layers, all on by default, no config needed: | Layer | What it does | |---|---| | **Protocol** | No `Runtime.enable` (defuses the DataDome console trap); CDP over WebSocket by default (native `webdriver=false`) with a zero-port pipe opt-in; isolated world for DOM reads. | | **Environment** | UA + Client Hints override (no HeadlessChrome); under Xvfb the lane renders on the real GPU (`--use-angle=gl-egl`) and reports the machine's own WebGL strings — the adaptive mask only exists for genuinely software hosts; mediaDevices, permissions — every override installed as a Proxy over the native original, so it keeps native receiver/argument errors, own keys `{length,name}`, no `prototype`, stringifies as native in **every** realm, and refuses the cyclic-prototype torture exactly like a native function (`TypeError: Cyclic __proto__ value` — creepjs's prototype lie engine reads 0). Nothing is fabricated: pages see the platform's real API surface and the display's real geometry. | | **Display** | A window manager on the virtual display (xfwm4): real frame extents (`outerWidth > innerWidth`), coherent outer/inner geometry, and the display's truthful work area — `availHeight` is the native value (a panel-less desktop reads `availHeight == height`, exactly like the machine's own session), no geometry getter is patched. Falls back to a self-correcting mask only on WM-less hosts. | | **Behavior** | Bezier mouse paths with overshoot + correction, `movementX/Y` deltas, micro-tremors, non-zero key-press duration, log-normal typing, idle hum, smooth scroll. | | **Coherence** | Per-domain timezone/locale memory, geo-consistent identity, WebRTC fail-closed, stable canvas/audio (noise off by default). | | **Residue** | `cdc_` remova

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
DeepSeek Harness Tauri 桌面版

在桌面上运行 DeepSeek Harness ——
无需手动安装 Node.js、pnpm 或 Docker；普通安装首次启动可能需要联网初始化。


Download · English · Español · 文档 · 中文

## 功能 - 🪶 **原生桌面** — Tauri 2 + React 19 + Hero 3，内嵌本地 Harness 界面。 - 📱 **远程连接** — 通过原生 Android / iOS 移动端连接电脑上的 DSH 实例。 - 🔄 **运行时管理** — 安装依赖、选择内核版本，并提供桌面端与内核更新入口。 - 🔀 **多内核支持** — 在同一界面畅用 DSH / Codex / Claude，发挥各自原生工具能力。 - 🧩 **插件管理** — 13 个内置插件；支持本地路径安装、内置插件停用、社区插件安装、升级、卸载与错误查看。 - 🗂️ **档案配置** — 分别管理插件与设置，支持一键迁移档案数据、备份、克隆； - 💽 **数据目录** — 安装时（Windows）可选择数据存放位置；能在设置里整体迁移与回滚。 - ⌨️ **命令行集成** — 通过托管 shim 提供 `dsh` / `pnpm` 命令行工具，不是全局 npm 内核安装。 - 🐾 **桌宠** — Pets / Codex 资源管理、资源包导入与会话状态展示；预设素材来自远端。 - 🎨 **个性化** — 8 种配色、本机界面缩放、终端模式，以及可调不透明度与可选磨砂模糊。 ## 内置插件 随桌面资源分发的一方插件： - [DSH Tauri](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri) — 核心插件，桌面端与 Harness 通信、版本适配器、插件依赖管理 - [DSH Tauri UI](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-ui) — 桌面设置界面、原生核心组件、主题与配色 - [DSH Tauri Mobile UI](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-mobile-ui) — 触屏布局与移动端偏好设置 - [DSH Tauri Kernel](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/tree/main/packages/dsh-tauri-kernel) — 本机 Codex / Claude 接入与模型选择 - [DSH Tauri Worktree](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-worktree) — 会话级 Git 工作树与检出 - [DSH Tauri Extension](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-extension) — 官方插件管理、插件市场、Skills 与 MCP - [DSH Tauri Scheduler](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-scheduler) — 定时任务与执行记录 - [DSH Tauri Archive](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-archive) — 聊天归档与恢复 - [DSH Tauri Pet](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-pet) — 桌宠与活动状态设置 - [DSH Tauri Rightclick Menu](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-rightclick) — 会话、工作区与正文右键菜单 - [DSH Tauri Model](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-model) — 模型选择与参数、自动配置模型 - [DSH Tauri Remote](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-remote) — SSH 远端 Harness 连接与同步，并把本机 Harness 分享到局域网或公网隧道 - [DSH Tauri Notification](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-notification) — 原生级会话通知与交互操作 ## 可选预设 启动引导提供以下社区插件，可按需安装； - [DSH Market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) — 社区插件市场 - [DSH Better Sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) — 按会话隔离的右编辑器侧栏 - [Billion Context](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — 上下文压缩与历史恢复 - [DSH Rewind](https://github.com/SiriLee/dsh-rewind) — 对话回退与工作区备份 - [DSH IM](https://github.com/xmanrui/dsh-im) — IM 渠道与机器人管理 新增或更新预设请提交 [Issue](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/issues)；可用版本由清单中的内核兼容规则决定。 ## 快速开始 从 [Releases](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/releases) 下载对应平台与架构的安装包： | 平台 | 要求 | 安装包 | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows | Windows 10+、WebView2 | x64 `.exe` / `.msi` | | macOS | macOS 12+；Web 界面需 Safari 17.4+ 能力 | Intel / Apple Silicon `.dmg` | | Linux | WebKit2GTK 4.1 运行库 | x64 `.AppImage` / `.deb` | macOS 也可通过 Homebrew 安装： ```bash brew install dsh-tauri/desktop/deepseek-harness ``` - 普通安装包首次启动需联网下载缺失的运行时与内核；Git 功能需要可用的 Git。 - 包含 `Bundle` 后缀为离线安装包（`_Bundle_*.exe`、`_Bundle_*.deb`、两种 `_Bundle_*.dmg`）。 - 本地运行不等于完全离线：模型服务、插件安装、更新与桌宠预设素材仍可能联网。 - Linux 显示、Wayland、AppImage 与权限问题的处理见[安装与故障排查文档](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/help/troubleshooting)。 ### 桌面代理 - 在**配置 → 应用 → 代理地址**设置 HTTP、HTTPS、SOCKS5 或 SOCKS5H 代理。 - 仅用于桌面端依赖/内核下载、更新检查及插件元数据，不修改模型请求或插件子进程的网络配置。 - 留空沿用系统/环境代理；保存后对新请求生效，可重试失败的下载。 - SOCKS5H 通过代理解析目标域名；本机回环连接始终直连。 ## 移动端支持 同一仓库内维护移动端 **DSH Mobile**（Expo / React Native）：在局域网发现 DSH 主机，并以全屏 WebView 承载 Harness 网页，源码位于 `src-native/`。 - Android APK 可在 [Releases](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/releases) 页面下载，资产名形如 `Deepseek.Harness.Android_x.x.x.apk`，版本跟随桌面端。 - **iOS 未签名 IPA 随桌面端发版**；需自行签名后安装，不能直接安装。 - 该移动端**仅在官方未推出移动端服务期间维护**，属于过渡方案。 - 开发命令（`pnpm dev:native`、`pnpm android`、`pnpm test:native`、`pnpm typecheck:native` 等）与发现、连接、持久化、发版约定见[移动端规范](docs/specs/native.md)。 ## 运行方式 Windows 启动失败时会通过原生对话框显示具体错误。若出现 `STARTUP_LOW_INTEGRITY`： - 进程低于 Medium 完整性级别，无法写入正常用户数据；更新后的程序可能继承安装目录的 Low 标签。 - 用 `icacls` 检查目录与程序；将可信安装恢复为 Medium，或重新安装到正常目录。 - 以管理员身份运行不会移除 Low 标签限制；无需删除会话或修改 `DSH_HOME`。 | 当前基线 | 版本 | | --- | --- | | 推荐 Harness 内核 | `0.2.0-rc.2` | | 声明的内核最低版本 | `0.1.5-rc.1`，不保证所有兼容 | - 内核与预设选择遵循[资源清单](<./src-tauri/resources/manifest.jsonc>)及插件声明的版本范围；不保证任意最新上游版本都兼容。 - 正式版默认启用 CLI 集成：Windows / macOS / Linux 自动更新 PATH。需重新打开终端，其他 shell 仍需要手动配置。 ## 交流

QQ 群
微信群(已满,请先加微信) →
微信
## 开发 参见[中文开发指南](<./docs/DEVELOPMENT.zh.md>)或[英文开发指南](<./docs/DEVELOPMENT.md>)。功能详情见[在线文档](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site)。 ## 说明 > [!WARNING] > **开发预览** — 上游 `dsh` 仍在快速迭代，可能存在破坏性变更；升级前请确认兼容性。 > [!NOTE] > **安全声明** — `dsh` 具备本地代码执行能力。仅供学习 / 研究 / 测试，请在可信、隔离的环境中使用。 ## 相关项目 - [deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — 上游 `dsh` agent 平台 - [deepseek-harness-pkg](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-pkg) — 预打包 Harness 发行版与下载源 - [dsh-pet](https://github.com/PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet) · [dsh-pet-mov](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/dsh-pet-mov) · [dsh-pet-component](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/dsh-pet-component) — 桌宠素材与渲染组件 - [dsh-plugin-codex-pets](https://github.com/Skylarking/dsh-plugin-codex-pets) · [BongoCat](https://github.com/ayangweb/BongoCat) · [dsh-dafeiyu](https://github.com/QCYTSN/dsh-dafeiyu) · [codex-to-dsh-pet](https://github.com/Signalight/codex-to-dsh-pet) — 桌宠参考项目 ## Contributors ![Contributors](https://contrib.rocks/image?repo=dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop) ## License [MIT](<./LICENSE>)，附加[非商用条款](<./LICENSE.details>) © deepseek-harness-desktop contributors

🐾 **桌宠** — Pets / Codex 资源管理、资源包导入与会话状态展示；预设素材来自远端。 - 🎨 **个性化** — 8 种配色、本机界面缩放、终端模式，以及可调不透明度与可选磨砂模糊。 ## 内置插件 随桌面资源分发的一方插件： - [DSH Tauri](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri) — 核心插件，桌面端与 Harness 通信、版本适配器、插件依赖管理 - [DSH Tauri UI](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-ui) — 桌面设置界面、原生核心组件、主题与配色 - [DSH Tauri Mobile UI](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-mobile-ui) — 触屏布局与移动端偏好设置 - [DSH Tauri Kernel](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/tree/main/packages/dsh-tauri-kernel) — 本机 Codex / Claude 接入与模型选择 - [DSH Tauri Worktree](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-worktree) — 会话级 Git 工作树与检出 - [DSH Tauri Extension](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-extension) — 官方插件管理、插件市场、Skills 与 MCP - [DSH Tauri Scheduler](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-scheduler) — 定时任务与执行记录 - [DSH Tauri Archive](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-archive) — 聊天归档与恢复 - [DSH Tauri Pet](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-pet) — 桌宠与活动状态设置 - [DSH Tauri Rightclick Menu](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-rightclick) — 会话、工作区与正文右键菜单 - [DSH Tauri Model](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-model) — 模型选择与参数、自动配置模型 - [DSH Tauri Remote](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-remote) — SSH 远端 Harness 连接与同步，并把本机 Harness 分享到局域网或公网隧道 - [DSH Tauri Notification](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-notification) — 原生级会话通知与交互操作 ## 可选预设 启动引导提供以下社区插件，可按需安装； - [DSH Market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) — 社区插件市场 - [DSH Better Sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) — 按会话隔离的右编辑器侧栏 - [Billion Context](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — 上下文压缩与历史恢复 - [DSH Rewind](https://github.com/SiriLee/dsh-rewind) — 对话回退与工作区备份 - [DSH IM](https://github.com/xmanrui/dsh-im) — IM 渠道与机器人管理 新增或更新预设请提交 [Issue](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/issues)；可用版本由清单中的内核兼容规则决定。 ## 快速开始 从 [Releases](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/releases) 下载对应平台与架构的安装包： | 平台 | 要求 | 安装包 | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows | Windows 10+、WebView2 | x64 `.exe` / `.msi` | | macOS | macOS 12+；Web 界面需 Safari 17.4+ 能力 | Intel / Apple Silicon `.dmg` | | Linux | WebKit2GTK 4.1 运行库 | x64 `.AppImage` / `.deb` | macOS 也可通过 Homebrew 安装： ```bash brew install dsh-tauri/desktop/deepseek-harness ``` - 普通安装包首次启动需联网下载缺失的运行时与内核；Git 功能需要可用的 Git。 - 包含 `Bundle` 后缀为离线安装包（`_Bundle_*.exe`、`_Bundle_*.deb`、两种 `_Bundle_*.dmg`）。 - 本地运行不等于完全离线：模型服务、插件安装、更新与桌宠预设素材仍可能联网。 - Linux 显示、Wayland、AppImage 与权限问题的处理见[安装与故障排查文档](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/help/troubleshooting)。 ### 桌面代理 - 在**配置 → 应用 → 代理地址**设置 HTTP、HTTPS、SOCKS5 或 SOCKS5H 代理。 - 仅用于桌面端依赖/内核下载、更新检查及插件元数据，不修改模型请求或插件子进程的网络配置。 - 留空沿用系统/环境代理；保存后对新请求生效，可重试失败的下载。 - SOCKS5H 通过代理解析目标域名；本机回环连接始终直连。 ## 移动端支持 同一仓库内维护移动端 **DSH Mobile**（Expo / React Native）：在局域网发现 DSH 主机，并以全屏 WebView 承载 Harness 网页，源码位于 `src-native/`。 - Android APK 可在 [Releases](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/releases) 页面下载，资产名形如 `Deepseek.Harness.Android_x.x.x.apk`，版本跟随桌面端。 - **iOS 未签名 IPA 随桌面端发版**；需自行签名后安装，不能直接安装。 - 该移动端**仅在官方未推出移动端服务期间维护**，属于过渡方案。 - 开发命令（`pnpm dev:native`、`pnpm android`、`pnpm test:native`、`pnpm typecheck:native` 等）与发现、连接、持久化、发版约定见[移动端规范](docs/specs/native.md)。 ## 运行方式 Windows 启动失败时会通过原生对话框显示具体错误。若出现 `STARTUP_LOW_INTEGRITY`： - 进程低于 Medium 完整性级别，无法写入正常用户数据；更新后的程序可能继承安装目录的 Low 标签。 - 用 `icacls` 检查目录与程序；将可信安装恢复为 Medium，或重新安装到正常目录。 - 以管理员身份运行不会移除 Low 标签限制；无需删除会话或修改 `DSH_HOME`。 | 当前基线 | 版本 | | --- | --- | | 推荐 Harness 内核 | `0.2.0-rc.2` | | 声明的内核最低版本 | `0.1.5-rc.1`，不保证所有兼容 | - 内核与预设选择遵循[资源清单](<./src-tauri/resources/manifest.jsonc>)及插件声明的版本范围；不保证任意最新上游版本都兼容。 - 正式版默认启用 CLI 集成：Windows / macOS / Linux 自动更新 PATH。需重新打开终端，其他 shell 仍需要手动配置。 ## 交流

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
DeepSeek Harness Tauri 桌面版

在桌面上运行 DeepSeek Harness ——
无需手动安装 Node.js、pnpm 或 Docker；普通安装首次启动可能需要联网初始化。


Download · English · Español · 文档 · 中文

## 功能 - 🪶 **原生桌面** — Tauri 2 + React 19 + Hero 3，内嵌本地 Harness 界面。 - 📱 **远程连接** — 通过原生 Android / iOS 移动端连接电脑上的 DSH 实例。 - 🔄 **运行时管理** — 安装依赖、选择内核版本，并提供桌面端与内核更新入口。 - 🔀 **多内核支持** — 在同一界面畅用 DSH / Codex / Claude，发挥各自原生工具能力。 - 🧩 **插件管理** — 13 个内置插件；支持本地路径安装、内置插件停用、社区插件安装、升级、卸载与错误查看。 - 🗂️ **档案配置** — 分别管理插件与设置，支持一键迁移档案数据、备份、克隆； - 💽 **数据目录** — 安装时（Windows）可选择数据存放位置；能在设置里整体迁移与回滚。 - ⌨️ **命令行集成** — 通过托管 shim 提供 `dsh` / `pnpm` 命令行工具，不是全局 npm 内核安装。 - 🐾 **桌宠** — Pets / Codex 资源管理、资源包导入与会话状态展示；预设素材来自远端。 - 🎨 **个性化** — 8 种配色、本机界面缩放、终端模式，以及可调不透明度与可选磨砂模糊。 ## 内置插件 随桌面资源分发的一方插件： - [DSH Tauri](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri) — 核心插件，桌面端与 Harness 通信、版本适配器、插件依赖管理 - [DSH Tauri UI](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-ui) — 桌面设置界面、原生核心组件、主题与配色 - [DSH Tauri Mobile UI](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-mobile-ui) — 触屏布局与移动端偏好设置 - [DSH Tauri Kernel](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/tree/main/packages/dsh-tauri-kernel) — 本机 Codex / Claude 接入与模型选择 - [DSH Tauri Worktree](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-worktree) — 会话级 Git 工作树与检出 - [DSH Tauri Extension](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-extension) — 官方插件管理、插件市场、Skills 与 MCP - [DSH Tauri Scheduler](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-scheduler) — 定时任务与执行记录 - [DSH Tauri Archive](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-archive) — 聊天归档与恢复 - [DSH Tauri Pet](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-pet) — 桌宠与活动状态设置 - [DSH Tauri Rightclick Menu](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-rightclick) — 会话、工作区与正文右键菜单 - [DSH Tauri Model](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-model) — 模型选择与参数、自动配置模型 - [DSH Tauri Remote](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-remote) — SSH 远端 Harness 连接与同步，并把本机 Harness 分享到局域网或公网隧道 - [DSH Tauri Notification](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-notification) — 原生级会话通知与交互操作 ## 可选预设 启动引导提供以下社区插件，可按需安装； - [DSH Market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) — 社区插件市场 - [DSH Better Sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) — 按会话隔离的右编辑器侧栏 - [Billion Context](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — 上下文压缩与历史恢复 - [DSH Rewind](https://github.com/SiriLee/dsh-rewind) — 对话回退与工作区备份 - [DSH IM](https://github.com/xmanrui/dsh-im) — IM 渠道与机器人管理 新增或更新预设请提交 [Issue](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/issues)；可用版本由清单中的内核兼容规则决定。 ## 快速开始 从 [Releases](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/releases) 下载对应平台与架构的安装包： | 平台 | 要求 | 安装包 | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows | Windows 10+、WebView2 | x64 `.exe` / `.msi` | | macOS | macOS 12+；Web 界面需 Safari 17.4+ 能力 | Intel / Apple Silicon `.dmg` | | Linux | WebKit2GTK 4.1 运行库 | x64 `.AppImage` / `.deb` | macOS 也可通过 Homebrew 安装： ```bash brew install dsh-tauri/desktop/deepseek-harness ``` - 普通安装包首次启动需联网下载缺失的运行时与内核；Git 功能需要可用的 Git。 - 包含 `Bundle` 后缀为离线安装包（`_Bundle_*.exe`、`_Bundle_*.deb`、两种 `_Bundle_*.dmg`）。 - 本地运行不等于完全离线：模型服务、插件安装、更新与桌宠预设素材仍可能联网。 - Linux 显示、Wayland、AppImage 与权限问题的处理见[安装与故障排查文档](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/help/troubleshooting)。 ### 桌面代理 - 在**配置 → 应用 → 代理地址**设置 HTTP、HTTPS、SOCKS5 或 SOCKS5H 代理。 - 仅用于桌面端依赖/内核下载、更新检查及插件元数据，不修改模型请求或插件子进程的网络配置。 - 留空沿用系统/环境代理；保存后对新请求生效，可重试失败的下载。 - SOCKS5H 通过代理解析目标域名；本机回环连接始终直连。 ## 移动端支持 同一仓库内维护移动端 **DSH Mobile**（Expo / React Native）：在局域网发现 DSH 主机，并以全屏 WebView 承载 Harness 网页，源码位于 `src-native/`。 - Android APK 可在 [Releases](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/releases) 页面下载，资产名形如 `Deepseek.Harness.Android_x.x.x.apk`，版本跟随桌面端。 - **iOS 未签名 IPA 随桌面端发版**；需自行签名后安装，不能直接安装。 - 该移动端**仅在官方未推出移动端服务期间维护**，属于过渡方案。 - 开发命令（`pnpm dev:native`、`pnpm android`、`pnpm test:native`、`pnpm typecheck:native` 等）与发现、连接、持久化、发版约定见[移动端规范](docs/specs/native.md)。 ## 运行方式 Windows 启动失败时会通过原生对话框显示具体错误。若出现 `STARTUP_LOW_INTEGRITY`： - 进程低于 Medium 完整性级别，无法写入正常用户数据；更新后的程序可能继承安装目录的 Low 标签。 - 用 `icacls` 检查目录与程序；将可信安装恢复为 Medium，或重新安装到正常目录。 - 以管理员身份运行不会移除 Low 标签限制；无需删除会话或修改 `DSH_HOME`。 | 当前基线 | 版本 | | --- | --- | | 推荐 Harness 内核 | `0.2.0-rc.2` | | 声明的内核最低版本 | `0.1.5-rc.1`，不保证所有兼容 | - 内核与预设选择遵循[资源清单](<./src-tauri/resources/manifest.jsonc>)及插件声明的版本范围；不保证任意最新上游版本都兼容。 - 正式版默认启用 CLI 集成：Windows / macOS / Linux 自动更新 PATH。需重新打开终端，其他 shell 仍需要手动配置。 ## 交流

QQ 群
微信群(已满,请先加微信) →
微信
## 开发 参见[中文开发指南](<./docs/DEVELOPMENT.zh.md>)或[英文开发指南](<./docs/DEVELOPMENT.md>)。功能详情见[在线文档](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site)。 ## 说明 > [!WARNING] > **开发预览** — 上游 `dsh` 仍在快速迭代，可能存在破坏性变更；升级前请确认兼容性。 > [!NOTE] > **安全声明** — `dsh` 具备本地代码执行能力。仅供学习 / 研究 / 测试，请在可信、隔离的环境中使用。 ## 相关项目 - [deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — 上游 `dsh` agent 平台 - [deepseek-harness-pkg](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-pkg) — 预打包 Harness 发行版与下载源 - [dsh-pet](https://github.com/PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet) · [dsh-pet-mov](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/dsh-pet-mov) · [dsh-pet-component](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/dsh-pet-component) — 桌宠素材与渲染组件 - [dsh-plugin-codex-pets](https://github.com/Skylarking/dsh-plugin-codex-pets) · [BongoCat](https://github.com/ayangweb/BongoCat) · [dsh-dafeiyu](https://github.com/QCYTSN/dsh-dafeiyu) · [codex-to-dsh-pet](https://github.com/Signalight/codex-to-dsh-pet) — 桌宠参考项目 ## Contributors ![Contributors](https://contrib.rocks/image?repo=dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop) ## License [MIT](<./LICENSE>)，附加[非商用条款](<./LICENSE.details>) © deepseek-harness-desktop contributors

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
DeepSeek Harness Tauri 桌面版

在桌面上运行 DeepSeek Harness ——
无需手动安装 Node.js、pnpm 或 Docker；普通安装首次启动可能需要联网初始化。


Download · English · Español · 文档 · 中文

## 功能 - 🪶 **原生桌面** — Tauri 2 + React 19 + Hero 3，内嵌本地 Harness 界面。 - 📱 **远程连接** — 通过原生 Android / iOS 移动端连接电脑上的 DSH 实例。 - 🔄 **运行时管理** — 安装依赖、选择内核版本，并提供桌面端与内核更新入口。 - 🔀 **多内核支持** — 在同一界面畅用 DSH / Codex / Claude，发挥各自原生工具能力。 - 🧩 **插件管理** — 13 个内置插件；支持本地路径安装、内置插件停用、社区插件安装、升级、卸载与错误查看。 - 🗂️ **档案配置** — 分别管理插件与设置，支持一键迁移档案数据、备份、克隆； - 💽 **数据目录** — 安装时（Windows）可选择数据存放位置；能在设置里整体迁移与回滚。 - ⌨️ **命令行集成** — 通过托管 shim 提供 `dsh` / `pnpm` 命令行工具，不是全局 npm 内核安装。 - 🐾 **桌宠** — Pets / Codex 资源管理、资源包导入与会话状态展示；预设素材来自远端。 - 🎨 **个性化** — 8 种配色、本机界面缩放、终端模式，以及可调不透明度与可选磨砂模糊。 ## 内置插件 随桌面资源分发的一方插件： - [DSH Tauri](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri) — 核心插件，桌面端与 Harness 通信、版本适配器、插件依赖管理 - [DSH Tauri UI](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-ui) — 桌面设置界面、原生核心组件、主题与配色 - [DSH Tauri Mobile UI](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-mobile-ui) — 触屏布局与移动端偏好设置 - [DSH Tauri Kernel](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/tree/main/packages/dsh-tauri-kernel) — 本机 Codex / Claude 接入与模型选择 - [DSH Tauri Worktree](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-worktree) — 会话级 Git 工作树与检出 - [DSH Tauri Extension](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-extension) — 官方插件管理、插件市场、Skills 与 MCP - [DSH Tauri Scheduler](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-scheduler) — 定时任务与执行记录 - [DSH Tauri Archive](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-archive) — 聊天归档与恢复 - [DSH Tauri Pet](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-pet) — 桌宠与活动状态设置 - [DSH Tauri Rightclick Menu](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-rightclick) — 会话、工作区与正文右键菜单 - [DSH Tauri Model](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-model) — 模型选择与参数、自动配置模型 - [DSH Tauri Remote](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-remote) — SSH 远端 Harness 连接与同步，并把本机 Harness 分享到局域网或公网隧道 - [DSH Tauri Notification](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-notification) — 原生级会话通知与交互操作 ## 可选预设 启动引导提供以下社区插件，可按需安装； - [DSH Market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) — 社区插件市场 - [DSH Better Sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) — 按会话隔离的右编辑器侧栏 - [Billion Context](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — 上下文压缩与历史恢复 - [DSH Rewind](https://github.com/SiriLee/dsh-rewind) — 对话回退与工作区备份 - [DSH IM](https://github.com/xmanrui/dsh-im) — IM 渠道与机器人管理 新增或更新预设请提交 [Issue](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/issues)；可用版本由清单中的内核兼容规则决定。 ## 快速开始 从 [Releases](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/releases) 下载对应平台与架构的安装包： | 平台 | 要求 | 安装包 | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows | Windows 10+、WebView2 | x64 `.exe` / `.msi` | | macOS | macOS 12+；Web 界面需 Safari 17.4+ 能力 | Intel / Apple Silicon `.dmg` | | Linux | WebKit2GTK 4.1 运行库 | x64 `.AppImage` / `.deb` | macOS 也可通过 Homebrew 安装： ```bash brew install dsh-tauri/desktop/deepseek-harness ``` - 普通安装包首次启动需联网下载缺失的运行时与内核；Git 功能需要可用的 Git。 - 包含 `Bundle` 后缀为离线安装包（`_Bundle_*.exe`、`_Bundle_*.deb`、两种 `_Bundle_*.dmg`）。 - 本地运行不等于完全离线：模型服务、插件安装、更新与桌宠预设素材仍可能联网。 - Linux 显示、Wayland、AppImage 与权限问题的处理见[安装与故障排查文档](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/help/troubleshooting)。 ### 桌面代理 - 在**配置 → 应用 → 代理地址**设置 HTTP、HTTPS、SOCKS5 或 SOCKS5H 代理。 - 仅用于桌面端依赖/内核下载、更新检查及插件元数据，不修改模型请求或插件子进程的网络配置。 - 留空沿用系统/环境代理；保存后对新请求生效，可重试失败的下载。 - SOCKS5H 通过代理解析目标域名；本机回环连接始终直连。 ## 移动端支持 同一仓库内维护移动端 **DSH Mobile**（Expo / React Native）：在局域网发现 DSH 主机，并以全屏 WebView 承载 Harness 网页，源码位于 `src-native/`。 - Android APK 可在 [Releases](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/releases) 页面下载，资产名形如 `Deepseek.Harness.Android_x.x.x.apk`，版本跟随桌面端。 - **iOS 未签名 IPA 随桌面端发版**；需自行签名后安装，不能直接安装。 - 该移动端**仅在官方未推出移动端服务期间维护**，属于过渡方案。 - 开发命令（`pnpm dev:native`、`pnpm android`、`pnpm test:native`、`pnpm typecheck:native` 等）与发现、连接、持久化、发版约定见[移动端规范](docs/specs/native.md)。 ## 运行方式 Windows 启动失败时会通过原生对话框显示具体错误。若出现 `STARTUP_LOW_INTEGRITY`： - 进程低于 Medium 完整性级别，无法写入正常用户数据；更新后的程序可能继承安装目录的 Low 标签。 - 用 `icacls` 检查目录与程序；将可信安装恢复为 Medium，或重新安装到正常目录。 - 以管理员身份运行不会移除 Low 标签限制；无需删除会话或修改 `DSH_HOME`。 | 当前基线 | 版本 | | --- | --- | | 推荐 Harness 内核 | `0.2.0-rc.2` | | 声明的内核最低版本 | `0.1.5-rc.1`，不保证所有兼容 | - 内核与预设选择遵循[资源清单](<./src-tauri/resources/manifest.jsonc>)及插件声明的版本范围；不保证任意最新上游版本都兼容。 - 正式版默认启用 CLI 集成：Windows / macOS / Linux 自动更新 PATH。需重新打开终端，其他 shell 仍需要手动配置。 ## 交流

普通安装包首次启动需联网下载缺失的运行时与内核；Git 功能需要可用的 Git。 - 包含 `Bundle` 后缀为离线安装包（`_Bundle_*.exe`、`_Bundle_*.deb`、两种 `_Bundle_*.dmg`）。 - 本地运行不等于完全离线：模型服务、插件安装、更新与桌宠预设素材仍可能联网。 - Linux 显示、Wayland、AppImage 与权限问题的处理见[安装与故障排查文档](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/help/troubleshooting)。 ### 桌面代理 - Android APK 可在 [Releases](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/releases) 页面下载，资产名形如 `Deepseek.Harness.Android_x.x.x.apk`，版本跟随桌面端。 - **iOS 未签名 IPA 随桌面端发版**；需自行签名后安装，不能直接安装。 - 该移动端**仅在官方未推出移动端服务期间维护**，属于过渡方案。 - 开发命令（`pnpm dev:native`、`pnpm android`、`pnpm test:native`、`pnpm typecheck:native` 等）与发现、连接、持久化、发版约定见[移动端规范](docs/specs/native.md)。 ## 运行方式 Windows 启动失败时会通过原生对话框显示具体错误。若出现 `STARTUP_LOW_INTEGRITY`： - 进程低于 Medium 完整性级别，无法写入正常用户数据；更新后的程序可能继承安装目录的 Low 标签。 - 🐾 **桌宠** — Pets / Codex 资源管理、资源包导入与会话状态展示；预设素材来自远端。 - 🎨 **个性化** — 8 种配色、本机界面缩放、终端模式，以及可调不透明度与可选磨砂模糊。 ## 内置插件 随桌面资源分发的一方插件： - [DSH Tauri](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri) — 核心插件，桌面端与 Harness 通信、版本适配器、插件依赖管理 - [DSH Tauri UI](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-ui) — 桌面设置界面、原生核心组件、主题与配色 - [DSH Tauri Mobile UI](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-mobile-ui) — 触屏布局与移动端偏好设置 - [DSH Tauri Kernel](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/tree/main/packages/dsh-tauri-kernel) — 本机 Codex / Claude 接入与模型选择 - [DSH Tauri Worktree](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-worktree) — 会话级 Git 工作树与检出 - [DSH Tauri Extension](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-extension) — 官方插件管理、插件市场、Skills 与 MCP - [DSH Tauri Scheduler](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-scheduler) — 定时任务与执行记录 - [DSH Tauri Archive](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-archive) — 聊天归档与恢复 - [DSH Tauri Pet](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-pet) — 桌宠与活动状态设置 - [DSH Tauri Rightclick Menu](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-rightclick) — 会话、工作区与正文右键菜单 - [DSH Tauri Model](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-model) — 模型选择与参数、自动配置模型 - [DSH Tauri Remote](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-remote) — SSH 远端 Harness 连接与同步，并把本机 Harness 分享到局域网或公网隧道 - [DSH Tauri Notification](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/built-in-plugins/dsh-tauri-notification) — 原生级会话通知与交互操作 ## 可选预设 启动引导提供以下社区插件，可按需安装； - [DSH Market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) — 社区插件市场 - [DSH Better Sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) — 按会话隔离的右编辑器侧栏 - [Billion Context](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — 上下文压缩与历史恢复 - [DSH Rewind](https://github.com/SiriLee/dsh-rewind) — 对话回退与工作区备份 - [DSH IM](https://github.com/xmanrui/dsh-im) — IM 渠道与机器人管理 新增或更新预设请提交 [Issue](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/issues)；可用版本由清单中的内核兼容规则决定。 ## 快速开始 从 [Releases](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/releases) 下载对应平台与架构的安装包： | 平台 | 要求 | 安装包 | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows | Windows 10+、WebView2 | x64 `.exe` / `.msi` | | macOS | macOS 12+；Web 界面需 Safari 17.4+ 能力 | Intel / Apple Silicon `.dmg` | | Linux | WebKit2GTK 4.1 运行库 | x64 `.AppImage` / `.deb` | macOS 也可通过 Homebrew 安装： ```bash brew install dsh-tauri/desktop/deepseek-harness ``` - 普通安装包首次启动需联网下载缺失的运行时与内核；Git 功能需要可用的 Git。 - 包含 `Bundle` 后缀为离线安装包（`_Bundle_*.exe`、`_Bundle_*.deb`、两种 `_Bundle_*.dmg`）。 - 本地运行不等于完全离线：模型服务、插件安装、更新与桌宠预设素材仍可能联网。 - Linux 显示、Wayland、AppImage 与权限问题的处理见[安装与故障排查文档](https://dshtauri.mintlify.site/zh-CN/help/troubleshooting)。 ### 桌面代理 - 在**配置 → 应用 → 代理地址**设置 HTTP、HTTPS、SOCKS5 或 SOCKS5H 代理。 - 仅用于桌面端依赖/内核下载、更新检查及插件元数据，不修改模型请求或插件子进程的网络配置。 - 留空沿用系统/环境代理；保存后对新请求生效，可重试失败的下载。 - SOCKS5H 通过代理解析目标域名；本机回环连接始终直连。 ## 移动端支持 同一仓库内维护移动端 **DSH Mobile**（Expo / React Native）：在局域网发现 DSH 主机，并以全屏 WebView 承载 Harness 网页，源码位于 `src-native/`。 - Android APK 可在 [Releases](https://github.com/dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop/releases) 页面下载，资产名形如 `Deepseek.Harness.Android_x.x.x.apk`，版本跟随桌面端。 - **iOS 未签名 IPA 随桌面端发版**；需自行签名后安装，不能直接安装。 - 该移动端**仅在官方未推出移动端服务期间维护**，属于过渡方案。 - 开发命令（`pnpm dev:native`、`pnpm android`、`pnpm test:native`、`pnpm typecheck:native` 等）与发现、连接、持久化、发版约定见[移动端规范](docs/specs/native.md)。 ## 运行方式 Windows 启动失败时会通过原生对话框显示具体错误。若出现 `STARTUP_LOW_INTEGRITY`： - 进程低于 Medium 完整性级别，无法写入正常用户数据；更新后的程序可能继承安装目录的 Low 标签。 - 用 `icacls` 检查目录与程序；将可信安装恢复为 Medium，或重新安装到正常目录。 - 以管理员身份运行不会移除 Low 标签限制；无需删除会话或修改 `DSH_HOME`。 | 当前基线 | 版本 | | --- | --- | | 推荐 Harness 内核 | `0.2.0-rc.2` | | 声明的内核最低版本 | `0.1.5-rc.1`，不保证所有兼容 | - 内核与预设选择遵循[资源清单](<./src-tauri/resources/manifest.jsonc>)及插件声明的版本范围；不保证任意最新上游版本都兼容。 - 正式版默认启用 CLI 集成：Windows / macOS / Linux 自动更新 PATH。需重新打开终端，其他 shell 仍需要手动配置。 ## 交流
