# @dsh-agentic-roleplay/state

The persistent session-state and memory service for DSH Agentic Roleplay, maintained by Firefox2100.

Most users should install [`@dsh-agentic-roleplay/all`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@dsh-agentic-roleplay/all). Install this package separately when another DSH plugin needs the roleplay database, repositories, recall engine, or model-facing record tools without the complete roleplay interface.

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that keeps the state of roleplay sessions: one SQLite
database per session, reached through repositories over canonical models. It
does no orchestration and has no UI, so it can be installed on its own to get a
roleplay database and state management without the rest of the roleplay bundle.
Other plugins use it through the `roleplayState` service. Model-facing tools
are included and can be enabled through its configuration.

Requires DSH 0.2 and Node 22.19 or later (it uses the built-in `node:sqlite`).

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add @dsh-agentic-roleplay/state
```

## Using it from another plugin

```ts
import type {} from '@dsh-agentic-roleplay/state'            // types `ctx.roleplayState`
import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'

export const inject = ['roleplayState']

export function apply(ctx: Context) {
  // Creates sessions/<uuid>/session.sqlite and opens it.
  const session = ctx.roleplayState.createSession('/path/to/sessions', {
    name: 'First night',
    world: { id: 'blackwater-observatory', name: 'The Blackwater Observatory' },
  })

  session.transaction(() => {
    const mayor = session.characters.add({ name: 'Eleanor Graves', /* … */ control: 'agent' })
    session.characterStates.create(mayor.id, { publicState: '…', innerState: '…', activity: '…' })
    session.intents.add(mayor.id, { type: 'agenda', name: '…', /* … */ })
  })

  session.characters.findByName('the mayor')       // by name or alias, ignoring case
  session.characterStates.update(1, { activity: 'looking for the key' }, { expectedVersion: 3 })
}
```

The service creates and opens sessions under a sessions folder you give it,
shares one connection per session, and closes them all when the plugin unloads:

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `createSession(sessionsDir, init)` | Creates the session folder and database and returns its repositories. The id is generated (UUID v4) unless given. Nothing is left behind if it fails. |
| `openSession(sessionsDir, id)` | Returns the repositories of an existing session. |
| `listSessions(sessionsDir)` | The metadata of every session under the folder (name, world, creation time, last played time, turns). A session that cannot be read is reported in `problems`, not thrown. |
| `closeSession(sessionsDir, id)` | Releases the connection; opening again reconnects. |
| `deleteSession(sessionsDir, id)` | Closes the session and removes its folder. |

Session ids become folder names, so only a UUID v4 is accepted. The package also
exports the same operations as plain functions (`createSession`, `openSession`,
`createSessionStore`, …) for code that does not run inside DSH, such as tests.

## The records API and the model-facing tools

The package owns how a story is remembered, not only where it is stored:

- `session.edit(edit)` changes the story's records (character states, events with who took each in, beliefs, threads) together or not at all. It checks the whole edit first and throws `InvalidEditError` naming every problem, so a model's mistakes can be reported back to it. `parseRecordsEdit(json)` reads the wire format models write (snake_case) and `recordsEditSchema({ characters, changes })` is its JSON schema, for a model's structured output or a tool's parameters.
- `session.records(scope)` reads the records back in the same wire format.
- `session.recall({ characterId, situation, turn, policy })` is what a character is reminded of: events it took in and things it believes, by who the situation mentions, shared words and tags, importance and story-time recency; with `policy.flaky` the older and less important are told as faded or vague, or are gone. Age is elapsed story time from `session.clock`, never turn count; an unimportant event has a six-story-day half-life. It counts what it brings back as recalled, which makes it last longer.
- `session.recallStored(query, { queryVector? })` adds the session's search index to the cues: texts that match the situation by words and, with the vector of the situation, by meaning. `session.searchEvents({ text, vector?, fromTurn, toTurn, minImportance, limit })` finds what happened by the same two searches, merged by reciprocal rank.
- `session.recallRanked(query, signal, { queryVector? })` is the call for anything that reminds a character of something: `recall`, ranked by meaning when a plugin has registered a ranker with `roleplayState.rankMemories(ranker)` (an embedding model, a reranker; see `docs/capabilities.md`). `session.recallCandidates(query)` gives what could be recalled, with the text to match, for a ranker. With `explain: true` in the query each recalled thing carries `why`: the cues of the moment (people named, words shared, place), what each search scored it, how much it matters, how long ago it was, how much of it is left in mind and what it was ranked by.
- `session.knowledge` is the closed-world awareness graph for locations, items and directed exits (`learn`, `knows`, `get`, `list`, `forget`). Directional relationships are the corresponding character-to-character edges. Awareness grants identity only, not current state or whereabouts. `session.planKnownMove` plans through only a character's known places and exits; `planMove` remains the authoritative world planner.
- `session.factions`, `factionStates`, `factionMemberships`, `factionRelationships` and `factionIntents` store persistent organisations separately from characters that act in scenes. Membership is many-to-many; relationships involving factions are directional and double as closed-world awareness edges.
- `roleplayState.bind(resolver)` tells the tools which roleplay session an agent works in (the plugin that runs the agents supplies it, with the turn being played and the memory policy).

Tools registered with the DSH tool registry (`defineTool`, typed output, honoring the call's `signal`), resolved through that binding: `list_characters`, `get_character`, `search_events`, `recall_memories`, `list_threads`, and, only when the plugin is configured with `writeTools: true`, `update_character_state`, `record_event`, `remember`, `open_thread`, `resolve_thread`. They fail with a plain message for an agent that works in no roleplay session. Characters and other one-shot sub-agents see none of them (they are started with no tools).

## Configuration

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `journalMode` | `delete` | `delete` keeps each session in a single file that can be copied; `wal` allows readers during writes. |
| `writeTools` | `false` | Also register the model-facing tools that change the records. Leave off where another agent is responsible for them. |

## Layers

| Layer | What it is |
|---|---|
| Canonical model | The types in `dsh-roleplay-model` (re-exported here): `Character`, `CharacterState`, `CharacterIntent`, `SessionMetadata`, … |
| Repositories | `MetadataRepository`, `CharacterRepository`, `CharacterStateRepository`, `IntentRepository`: the only access to the data. They take and return canonical models and throw the errors below. |
| SQLite implementation | Maps rows to models and back; the only place that knows tables and SQL. |
| Driver | `SqlDriver` / `SqlDatabase`: the few operations the implementation needs (`exec`, `run`, `get`, `all`, `transaction`). `nodeSqliteDriver` is built on `node:sqlite`. |

Everything is synchronous, as the embedded SQLite libraries are.

This is an independent community project, not an official DSH package. [Documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-agentic-roleplay/docs/developers/state) · [Source](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-agentic-roleplay) · [Issues](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-agentic-roleplay/issues) · GPL-3.0-only

## The session

A session is the folder `sessions/<uuid>/` with its database `session.sqlite`.
The database is the only file the state needs; with the default journal mode it
stays a single file that can be copied or archived.

The world itself is not stored. `metadata` keeps a **world reference**: the
world's stable id (the `id` in its `world.json`, not a database id), its name,
and optionally a version, a fingerprint of the content the session was started
from, its source, and free-form `extra` fields. It is saved as one document, so
provenance can grow without a schema change.

The metadata also carries what a list of sessions shows: the session's `name`
(chosen when it is created), its creation time, the time of the last play
(absent until a turn has been played) and the number of turns played. Whatever
plays a turn calls `metadata.recordTurn()`, which counts it and sets the time.

Characters have session-local integer ids. `source_id` keeps the id the
character had in the world, so a session can be traced back to its world;
characters created during play have none.

## Schema (version 1)

| Table | Holds |
|---|---|
| `metadata` | Key/value rows: `session.id`, `session.name`, `session.created_at`, `session.last_played_at`, `session.turns`, `world` (JSON), plus free-form namespaced entries. |
| `characters` | The definition: name, age, gender, pronouns, kind, tier, role, summary, personality, background, appearance, speech, and `control` (`player` or `agent`, chosen for the session). `source_id` is unique. |
| `character_aliases` | One row per alias, in order, with a case-folded key for lookup. |
| `character_state` | The state that changes in play: public state, inner state, activity, `version`, `updated_at`. One row per character. |
| `character_emotion` | Optional baseline and immediate valence/arousal/dominance of a state. |
| `intents` | A character's intents: type, name, description, status, horizon, priority, urgency, plan, open threads, constraints, deadline. |
| `relationships`, `consolidation_items` | How a character stands towards another (a profile per direction: label, summary, familiarity, trust, affinity, tension) and the characters and places made up in play that still have to be fitted into the world. `lintWorld` reports what is inconsistent. The edit can make characters, places and ways when it is the authoring variant (`recordsEditSchema({ authoring: true })`). |
| `entity_knowledge` | Explicit character-to-location/item/exit awareness: the first learned turn and optional last directly observed turn. Absence means unknown; current facts remain in state, perception and memory. |
| `factions`, `faction_aliases`, `faction_state`, `faction_memberships`, `faction_relationships`, `faction_intents` | Organisations, their institutional state and strategy, many-to-many membership, and directional relationships involving a faction. |
| `slots`, `items`, `item_holdings`, `openers`, `event_items` | Things (one kind for items, equipment and containers: quantity, condition, notable, hidden, the slot it is worn in, a container state, an owner), where each is (a place, a character's hands or a slot, or inside a container item), the places on the body something can be worn (with defaults, data per session), what opens each lock (on items and exits), and which events are about which items. `changeItem` does what a character does with a thing (take, drop, give, put, wear, remove, open, close, lock, unlock, reveal) by the rules of the story and says every reason when it cannot. |
| `clock`, `time_log` | The story's own time: one row with the mode (`simulated` or `real`) and the instant, and every step it took (start, elapsed, real, skip, resync) with the turn and round. `session.clock` starts it, moves it forward, sets it in either direction when the mode changes, and tells when a round began. |
| `routine_windows`, `engagements`, `engagement_participants` | The recurring day of each character (windows of the day with what it is doing and where, first fit applies) and dated commitments with who made them and whether they were kept. `session.routines` and `session.engagements`; `agendaAt` merges them with the character's goals (`intents`). |
| `locations`, `exits`, `placements` | Places (with features), the ways between them (one direction each, `open` / `locked` / `blocked`, optional travel seconds) and where things stand (a character: place, position, feature; the same table will place items). `session.planMove` / `session.move` move a character over open exits only (`InvalidMoveError` names every reason); the edit wire format can make places, change exits and move characters. |
| `events` | What objectively happened: turn, round, text, importance (1 to 5), tags. `event_involves` lists the characters an event is about. Events are immutable: a draft until `sealed`, final afterwards (`events.seal()`); updating or removing a sealed one throws `ConflictError`. |
| `perceptions` | What one character took in of an event, in its own terms: mode (witnessed, heard, told, inferred), content, a gist for when it fades, an accuracy label (never shown to the character), and how often it was recalled. One per character and event. |
| `memories` | What a character believes or knows beyond single events: kind (belief, relationship, knowledge), text, the characters it is about, importance, the turn it formed in. |
| `story_threads` | Things not settled yet: promises, mysteries, goals; open or resolved. |
| `summaries` | The account of the story for the conversation's head: digests of recent turns and chapters of older ones, each with the turns it covers. |
| `recall_items`, `recall_fts`, `recall_vocab`, `recall_vec` | The search index: one row per perception, memory and event, indexed by words (FTS5) and, once vectors are stored, by meaning (sqlite-vec, cosine, partitioned by character). `store.recallIndex` lists the texts without a vector (`pending`), stores vectors (`store`, which fixes the model and dimensions of the session's vectors) and searches (`lexical`, `vector`). Vector support is optional: without the extension everything but `vector` works. |
| `pending_commits` | Recorded rounds whose events and memories are not written yet, kept so that a failure loses nothing. |

Events are the ground truth; perceptions (which stay revisable: `updatePerception`, `addPerception`), memories and summaries are derived from them and can be rebuilt. The repositories are `events`, `memories`, `threads`, `summaries` and `pendingCommits` next to the ones for characters.

Deleting a character deletes everything that belongs to it. The tables are
`STRICT`, enumerations and ranges are `CHECK` constraints, and foreign keys are
enforced. The file records its schema version in `user_version` and carries an
application id, so a file that is not a session database is refused.

## Changing the schema

Migrations are applied in order when a session is opened and are never edited
once released: a change is a new entry in `src/sqlite/schema.ts`, and a test
pins the migrations of each release. A database from a newer version is refused
rather than damaged.

Before a file that is behind the latest schema is upgraded, it must pass SQLite's
quick integrity check (a damaged file is refused with `CorruptDataError`, untouched)
and a copy of it as it was is written to `migration-backups/schema-<version>.sqlite`
beside the database, once per old version. `migrationBackupPath(location, version)`
says where.

## Errors

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `NotFoundError` | A row, character or session file does not exist. |
| `ConflictError` | A repeated `source_id`, a state created twice, a stale `expectedVersion`, or creating a session where one exists. |
| `InvalidValueError` | A value is outside what the schema allows. |
| `SchemaError` | The file is not a session database, or comes from a newer version. |
| `CorruptDataError` | Stored data cannot be read back as a model. |

# DSH Agentic Roleplay

Persistent, agent-driven roleplay for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-Harness). Create a world, choose who to play, and enter an evolving story whose characters can make decisions of their own.

Instead of treating roleplay as one long prompt, the bundle separates the game master, character decisions, record keeping, world authoring, and media work. The story keeps structured state for what happened, what each character perceived and remembers, where people and things are, how relationships change, and which possibilities remain open.

## What makes it different

- **Characters have their own point of view.** They act from their goals, relationships, knowledge, memories, and current situation—not from everything stored in the world.
- **The world changes without becoming a script.** Plots can provide direction and pressure, while player choices and autonomous character actions determine what actually happens.
- **Stories remain editable and durable.** Worlds are filesystem-first, sessions use SQLite, and branching or taking back does not require rebuilding the setting.
- **Creation happens inside DSH.** Build worlds in the editor, ask an approval-gated authoring agent for help, import character cards, and generate portraits or scene illustrations when providers are available.
- **Media is optional.** Text play works without image, speech, embedding, or reranking services; add them when you want portraits, voiced scenes, voice input, or richer recall.

The bundle includes a complete roleplay interface, a bounded game-master loop, autonomous character and faction activity, story-time memory, relationships and knowledge, locations and items, plots and triggers, reusable avatars, world authoring, speech, and image workflows.

This project is independently maintained by [Firefox2100](https://github.com/Firefox2100). It is not an official DeepSeek Harness project.

## Documentation

- [English documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-agentic-roleplay/docs/intro)
- [简体中文文档](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-agentic-roleplay/zh-Hans/docs/intro)
- [Installation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-agentic-roleplay/docs/getting-started/installation)
- [World authoring](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-agentic-roleplay/docs/authoring/overview)
- [World format](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-agentic-roleplay/docs/world-format/overview)
- [Plugin development](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-agentic-roleplay/docs/developers/architecture)
- [Maintainer guide](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-agentic-roleplay/docs/maintainers/overview)

## Packages

| Package | Role |
|---|---|
| `@dsh-agentic-roleplay/all` | Installable bundle containing the complete experience. |
| `@dsh-agentic-roleplay/core` | UI, orchestration, authoring, media, and filesystem integration. |
| `@dsh-agentic-roleplay/state` | Standalone DSH service for session databases, repositories, recall, and model-facing record tools. |
| `dsh-roleplay-model` | Private canonical model package, bundled into the published plugins. |

## Installation

Install the complete bundle into a DSH profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-agentic-roleplay/all
```

Restart the profile, then configure the storage root under **Settings → Role Play**. AI features are supplied by compatible provider plugins; see [AI services](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-agentic-roleplay/docs/getting-started/ai-services).

New users can add the included *Blackwater Observatory* sample world from the Worlds page, inspect how it is built, and begin a session immediately after configuring a language model.

## Development

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run test
pnpm run build
```

Requires Node.js 22 or later and pnpm. See the [maintainer guide](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-agentic-roleplay/docs/maintainers/overview) before changing persisted data, the agent loop, prompts, or DSH integration.

# @dsh-ai-providers/all

The complete AI provider foundation for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), maintained by Firefox2100 as part of the dsh-ai-providers project.

It installs the shared runtime plus the OpenAI, LocalAI, Anthropic, and Jina/Cohere provider plugins. Users configure each connection and DSH-managed credential once, then plugins can reuse it across language models, retrieval, speech, and image generation.

This package contains bundle metadata only; it has no JavaScript API. Installing it alone does not add an assistant or make AI requests. It supplies capabilities to other DSH plugins that consume the shared services. More providers and services are planned for later releases.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/all
```

Use the DSH settings interface to configure credentials, connections, models, capability routing, and concurrency limits after installation.

When using its language-model routes, disable DSH's stock model adapter and Models settings page, but keep the core `llm` service. For DSH Voice Input, select the API-backed transcription provider instead of the built-in SenseVoice provider.

This is an independent community project. It is not an official DSH package and is not maintained or endorsed by the DSH maintainers.

[Documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/intro) · [Installation guide](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/installation) · [Source](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-ai-providers) · [Issues](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-ai-providers/issues)

Licensed under GPL-3.0-only.

# DSH AI Providers

Reusable, provider-neutral AI services for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/DeepSeek-AI/DeepSeek-Harness).

DSH AI Providers is infrastructure for plugins that need AI capabilities beyond a single model backend. Users register a vendor connection and credential once, then reuse it for every capability that vendor supplies. Consumer plugins call stable services instead of implementing credentials, provider selection, concurrency control, and vendor APIs themselves.

It currently covers:

- language models;
- embeddings and reranking;
- text-to-speech and speech-to-text;
- image generation.

The project is primarily useful to plugin developers and to users of plugins built on it. Installing it alone does not add an assistant or start making AI requests: configure the providers you need, then install or build a plugin that consumes the services.

## Why use it

- Configure a connection and DSH-managed credential once instead of repeating secrets in every feature or plugin.
- Let users choose or change providers without coupling consumer plugins to vendor-specific APIs.
- Share capability contracts, live configuration, and concurrency limits across plugins.
- Retain vendor-specific controls where a common interface would otherwise hide useful behavior.

Additional vendor packages and services will be added as the ecosystem grows. The provider-neutral contracts are the foundation: existing consumer plugins should not need to be redesigned for every new backend.

## Documentation

- [Documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/intro)
- [简体中文文档](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/zh-Hans/docs/intro)
- [Installation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/installation)
- [Configuration](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/configuration)
- [Using services from another plugin](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/consumers/using-services)
- [Creating a provider package](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/providers/creating-provider)

## Packages

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/core` | Provider-neutral service contracts, errors, and shared types |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/openai-compatible` | Reusable OpenAI-compatible wire transports; not a plugin |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/runtime` | Provider registry, service selection, concurrency control, API routes, and settings UI |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/openai` | OpenAI-compatible language models, embeddings, TTS, file and live STT, and image generation |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/localai` | LocalAI language models, embeddings, reranking, TTS, file and live STT, and image generation |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/anthropic` | Language models through Anthropic's native Messages API |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/jina-cohere` | Reranking through Jina- and Cohere-compatible APIs |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/all` | Metadata-only DSH bundle containing the runtime and every provider maintained by this project |

See the individual provider guides for configuration and supported features:

- [OpenAI-compatible](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/openai)
- [LocalAI](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/localai)
- [Anthropic](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/anthropic)
- [Jina and Cohere](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/jina-cohere)

## Installation

Install the bundle into a DSH profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/all
```

The bundle installs the runtime and all vendor packages maintained by this project. Restart the profile, then configure connections, routes, and active services under **Settings → AI Providers**. Individual packages may also be installed separately for a custom deployment.

To use these language-model routes in place of DSH's stock routes, disable `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` and the stock `ui-settings-models` settings page in that profile. Keep DSH's core `llm` service enabled. For DSH Voice Input, keep its speech-to-text registry enabled but select the API-backed provider instead of the built-in SenseVoice provider.

This is an independent project maintained by Firefox2100. It is not an official DeepSeek Harness project and is not maintained or endorsed by the DSH maintainers.

## Development

Requires Node.js 22 or later and pnpm.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run test
pnpm run build
pnpm run release:check
```

See [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for branch and release policy.

## License

[GPL-3.0-only](./LICENSE)

decision.reason: Held for versioned DSH compatibility, package or companion artifact mapping. GPL-3.0-only bundle mounts native runtime/OpenAI/Anthropic/Jina-Cohere/LocalAI components. Repository identity is consistent, but companion artifacts and versioned DSH contract remain unresolved. Provider credentials and model data cross external network boundaries. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# @dsh-ai-providers/anthropic

Native Anthropic Messages API language model support for DeepSeek Harness.

The plugin plugs Anthropic into the shared runtime, so users configure a connection and DSH-managed credential once and consumer plugins can reuse it. It provides model routes, streaming responses, vision, tool use, reasoning content, usage reporting, and Anthropic-native request controls.

Installing it alone does not add an assistant or invoke Anthropic; a consumer plugin must use its model route.

## Install

Install [`@dsh-ai-providers/all`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@dsh-ai-providers/all) for the complete project-maintained bundle, or add this package alongside the runtime in a custom deployment:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/runtime
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/anthropic
```

The runtime command activates the shared registry and settings surface. Installing this package also downloads the runtime as a package dependency, but DSH activates bundle layers explicitly, so both commands are required.

[Provider documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/anthropic) · [Configuration](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/configuration) · [Source](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-ai-providers) · [Issues](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-ai-providers/issues)

Licensed under GPL-3.0-only.

# DSH AI Providers

Reusable, provider-neutral AI services for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/DeepSeek-AI/DeepSeek-Harness).

DSH AI Providers is infrastructure for plugins that need AI capabilities beyond a single model backend. Users register a vendor connection and credential once, then reuse it for every capability that vendor supplies. Consumer plugins call stable services instead of implementing credentials, provider selection, concurrency control, and vendor APIs themselves.

It currently covers:

- language models;
- embeddings and reranking;
- text-to-speech and speech-to-text;
- image generation.

The project is primarily useful to plugin developers and to users of plugins built on it. Installing it alone does not add an assistant or start making AI requests: configure the providers you need, then install or build a plugin that consumes the services.

## Why use it

- Configure a connection and DSH-managed credential once instead of repeating secrets in every feature or plugin.
- Let users choose or change providers without coupling consumer plugins to vendor-specific APIs.
- Share capability contracts, live configuration, and concurrency limits across plugins.
- Retain vendor-specific controls where a common interface would otherwise hide useful behavior.

Additional vendor packages and services will be added as the ecosystem grows. The provider-neutral contracts are the foundation: existing consumer plugins should not need to be redesigned for every new backend.

## Documentation

- [Documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/intro)
- [简体中文文档](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/zh-Hans/docs/intro)
- [Installation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/installation)
- [Configuration](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/configuration)
- [Using services from another plugin](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/consumers/using-services)
- [Creating a provider package](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/providers/creating-provider)

## Packages

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/core` | Provider-neutral service contracts, errors, and shared types |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/openai-compatible` | Reusable OpenAI-compatible wire transports; not a plugin |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/runtime` | Provider registry, service selection, concurrency control, API routes, and settings UI |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/openai` | OpenAI-compatible language models, embeddings, TTS, file and live STT, and image generation |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/localai` | LocalAI language models, embeddings, reranking, TTS, file and live STT, and image generation |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/anthropic` | Language models through Anthropic's native Messages API |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/jina-cohere` | Reranking through Jina- and Cohere-compatible APIs |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/all` | Metadata-only DSH bundle containing the runtime and every provider maintained by this project |

See the individual provider guides for configuration and supported features:

- [OpenAI-compatible](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/openai)
- [LocalAI](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/localai)
- [Anthropic](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/anthropic)
- [Jina and Cohere](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/jina-cohere)

## Installation

Install the bundle into a DSH profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/all
```

The bundle installs the runtime and all vendor packages maintained by this project. Restart the profile, then configure connections, routes, and active services under **Settings → AI Providers**. Individual packages may also be installed separately for a custom deployment.

To use these language-model routes in place of DSH's stock routes, disable `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` and the stock `ui-settings-models` settings page in that profile. Keep DSH's core `llm` service enabled. For DSH Voice Input, keep its speech-to-text registry enabled but select the API-backed provider instead of the built-in SenseVoice provider.

This is an independent project maintained by Firefox2100. It is not an official DeepSeek Harness project and is not maintained or endorsed by the DSH maintainers.

## Development

Requires Node.js 22 or later and pnpm.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run test
pnpm run build
pnpm run release:check
```

See [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for branch and release policy.

## License

# @dsh-ai-providers/jina-cohere

Reranking through Jina- and Cohere-compatible APIs for DeepSeek Harness.

The plugin supports the common `/rerank` request shape used by Jina AI, Cohere, and compatible services. Users configure connections and DSH-managed credentials once, while model and request defaults remain provider-specific. Any consumer plugin using the shared reranking service can then use the selected backend.

Installing it alone does not perform retrieval or reranking; a consumer plugin must request the service.

## Install

Install [`@dsh-ai-providers/all`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@dsh-ai-providers/all) for the complete project-maintained bundle, or add this package alongside the runtime in a custom deployment:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/runtime
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/jina-cohere
```

The runtime command activates the shared registry and settings surface. Installing this package also downloads the runtime as a package dependency, but DSH activates bundle layers explicitly, so both commands are required.

[Provider documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/jina-cohere) · [Configuration](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/configuration) · [Source](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-ai-providers) · [Issues](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-ai-providers/issues)

Licensed under GPL-3.0-only.

# DSH AI Providers

Reusable, provider-neutral AI services for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/DeepSeek-AI/DeepSeek-Harness).

DSH AI Providers is infrastructure for plugins that need AI capabilities beyond a single model backend. Users register a vendor connection and credential once, then reuse it for every capability that vendor supplies. Consumer plugins call stable services instead of implementing credentials, provider selection, concurrency control, and vendor APIs themselves.

It currently covers:

- language models;
- embeddings and reranking;
- text-to-speech and speech-to-text;
- image generation.

The project is primarily useful to plugin developers and to users of plugins built on it. Installing it alone does not add an assistant or start making AI requests: configure the providers you need, then install or build a plugin that consumes the services.

## Why use it

- Configure a connection and DSH-managed credential once instead of repeating secrets in every feature or plugin.
- Let users choose or change providers without coupling consumer plugins to vendor-specific APIs.
- Share capability contracts, live configuration, and concurrency limits across plugins.
- Retain vendor-specific controls where a common interface would otherwise hide useful behavior.

Additional vendor packages and services will be added as the ecosystem grows. The provider-neutral contracts are the foundation: existing consumer plugins should not need to be redesigned for every new backend.

## Documentation

- [Documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/intro)
- [简体中文文档](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/zh-Hans/docs/intro)
- [Installation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/installation)
- [Configuration](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/configuration)
- [Using services from another plugin](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/consumers/using-services)
- [Creating a provider package](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/providers/creating-provider)

## Packages

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/core` | Provider-neutral service contracts, errors, and shared types |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/openai-compatible` | Reusable OpenAI-compatible wire transports; not a plugin |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/runtime` | Provider registry, service selection, concurrency control, API routes, and settings UI |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/openai` | OpenAI-compatible language models, embeddings, TTS, file and live STT, and image generation |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/localai` | LocalAI language models, embeddings, reranking, TTS, file and live STT, and image generation |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/anthropic` | Language models through Anthropic's native Messages API |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/jina-cohere` | Reranking through Jina- and Cohere-compatible APIs |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/all` | Metadata-only DSH bundle containing the runtime and every provider maintained by this project |

See the individual provider guides for configuration and supported features:

- [OpenAI-compatible](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/openai)
- [LocalAI](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/localai)
- [Anthropic](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/anthropic)
- [Jina and Cohere](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/jina-cohere)

## Installation

Install the bundle into a DSH profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/all
```

The bundle installs the runtime and all vendor packages maintained by this project. Restart the profile, then configure connections, routes, and active services under **Settings → AI Providers**. Individual packages may also be installed separately for a custom deployment.

To use these language-model routes in place of DSH's stock routes, disable `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` and the stock `ui-settings-models` settings page in that profile. Keep DSH's core `llm` service enabled. For DSH Voice Input, keep its speech-to-text registry enabled but select the API-backed provider instead of the built-in SenseVoice provider.

This is an independent project maintained by Firefox2100. It is not an official DeepSeek Harness project and is not maintained or endorsed by the DSH maintainers.

## Development

Requires Node.js 22 or later and pnpm.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run test
pnpm run build
pnpm run release:check
```

See [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for branch and release policy.

## License

# @dsh-ai-providers/localai

First-class LocalAI language model, embedding, reranking, speech, and image generation services for DeepSeek Harness, including LocalAI-specific controls.

It lets users configure a LocalAI connection and credential once, then reuse them across consumer plugins and capabilities. It supports LocalAI's OpenAI-compatible endpoints while retaining LocalAI-specific sampling fields, request bodies, defaults, and native reranking. It shares only the neutral wire implementation with the OpenAI provider and does not depend on that plugin.

Installing it alone does not start LocalAI or make requests; a consumer plugin must request one of the services.

## Install

Install [`@dsh-ai-providers/all`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@dsh-ai-providers/all) for the complete project-maintained bundle, or add this package alongside the runtime in a custom deployment:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/runtime
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/localai
```

The runtime command activates the shared registry and settings surface. Installing this package also downloads the runtime as a package dependency, but DSH activates bundle layers explicitly, so both commands are required.

[Provider documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/localai) · [Configuration](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/configuration) · [Source](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-ai-providers) · [Issues](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-ai-providers/issues)

Licensed under GPL-3.0-only.

# DSH AI Providers

Reusable, provider-neutral AI services for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/DeepSeek-AI/DeepSeek-Harness).

DSH AI Providers is infrastructure for plugins that need AI capabilities beyond a single model backend. Users register a vendor connection and credential once, then reuse it for every capability that vendor supplies. Consumer plugins call stable services instead of implementing credentials, provider selection, concurrency control, and vendor APIs themselves.

It currently covers:

- language models;
- embeddings and reranking;
- text-to-speech and speech-to-text;
- image generation.

The project is primarily useful to plugin developers and to users of plugins built on it. Installing it alone does not add an assistant or start making AI requests: configure the providers you need, then install or build a plugin that consumes the services.

## Why use it

- Configure a connection and DSH-managed credential once instead of repeating secrets in every feature or plugin.
- Let users choose or change providers without coupling consumer plugins to vendor-specific APIs.
- Share capability contracts, live configuration, and concurrency limits across plugins.
- Retain vendor-specific controls where a common interface would otherwise hide useful behavior.

Additional vendor packages and services will be added as the ecosystem grows. The provider-neutral contracts are the foundation: existing consumer plugins should not need to be redesigned for every new backend.

## Documentation

- [Documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/intro)
- [简体中文文档](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/zh-Hans/docs/intro)
- [Installation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/installation)
- [Configuration](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/configuration)
- [Using services from another plugin](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/consumers/using-services)
- [Creating a provider package](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/providers/creating-provider)

## Packages

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/core` | Provider-neutral service contracts, errors, and shared types |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/openai-compatible` | Reusable OpenAI-compatible wire transports; not a plugin |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/runtime` | Provider registry, service selection, concurrency control, API routes, and settings UI |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/openai` | OpenAI-compatible language models, embeddings, TTS, file and live STT, and image generation |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/localai` | LocalAI language models, embeddings, reranking, TTS, file and live STT, and image generation |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/anthropic` | Language models through Anthropic's native Messages API |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/jina-cohere` | Reranking through Jina- and Cohere-compatible APIs |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/all` | Metadata-only DSH bundle containing the runtime and every provider maintained by this project |

See the individual provider guides for configuration and supported features:

- [OpenAI-compatible](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/openai)
- [LocalAI](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/localai)
- [Anthropic](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/anthropic)
- [Jina and Cohere](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/jina-cohere)

## Installation

Install the bundle into a DSH profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/all
```

The bundle installs the runtime and all vendor packages maintained by this project. Restart the profile, then configure connections, routes, and active services under **Settings → AI Providers**. Individual packages may also be installed separately for a custom deployment.

To use these language-model routes in place of DSH's stock routes, disable `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` and the stock `ui-settings-models` settings page in that profile. Keep DSH's core `llm` service enabled. For DSH Voice Input, keep its speech-to-text registry enabled but select the API-backed provider instead of the built-in SenseVoice provider.

This is an independent project maintained by Firefox2100. It is not an official DeepSeek Harness project and is not maintained or endorsed by the DSH maintainers.

## Development

Requires Node.js 22 or later and pnpm.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run test
pnpm run build
pnpm run release:check
```

See [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for branch and release policy.

# @dsh-ai-providers/openai

OpenAI-compatible language model, embedding, text-to-speech, file and live speech-to-text, and image generation services for DeepSeek Harness.

The plugin plugs these capabilities into the shared runtime, so users configure an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and DSH-managed credential once and consumer plugins can reuse them. It provides model discovery, streaming tool-capable chat, and per-capability configuration. It uses [`@dsh-ai-providers/openai-compatible`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@dsh-ai-providers/openai-compatible) for the shared protocol implementation.

Installing it alone does not add an assistant or invoke OpenAI; a consumer plugin must request one of the services.

## Install

Install [`@dsh-ai-providers/all`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@dsh-ai-providers/all) for the complete project-maintained bundle, or add this package alongside the runtime in a custom deployment:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/runtime
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/openai
```

The runtime command activates the shared registry and settings surface. Installing this package also downloads the runtime as a package dependency, but DSH activates bundle layers explicitly, so both commands are required.

[Provider documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/openai) · [Configuration](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/configuration) · [Source](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-ai-providers) · [Issues](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-ai-providers/issues)

Licensed under GPL-3.0-only.

# DSH AI Providers

Reusable, provider-neutral AI services for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/DeepSeek-AI/DeepSeek-Harness).

DSH AI Providers is infrastructure for plugins that need AI capabilities beyond a single model backend. Users register a vendor connection and credential once, then reuse it for every capability that vendor supplies. Consumer plugins call stable services instead of implementing credentials, provider selection, concurrency control, and vendor APIs themselves.

It currently covers:

- language models;
- embeddings and reranking;
- text-to-speech and speech-to-text;
- image generation.

The project is primarily useful to plugin developers and to users of plugins built on it. Installing it alone does not add an assistant or start making AI requests: configure the providers you need, then install or build a plugin that consumes the services.

## Why use it

- Configure a connection and DSH-managed credential once instead of repeating secrets in every feature or plugin.
- Let users choose or change providers without coupling consumer plugins to vendor-specific APIs.
- Share capability contracts, live configuration, and concurrency limits across plugins.
- Retain vendor-specific controls where a common interface would otherwise hide useful behavior.

Additional vendor packages and services will be added as the ecosystem grows. The provider-neutral contracts are the foundation: existing consumer plugins should not need to be redesigned for every new backend.

## Documentation

- [Documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/intro)
- [简体中文文档](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/zh-Hans/docs/intro)
- [Installation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/installation)
- [Configuration](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/configuration)
- [Using services from another plugin](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/consumers/using-services)
- [Creating a provider package](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/providers/creating-provider)

## Packages

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/core` | Provider-neutral service contracts, errors, and shared types |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/openai-compatible` | Reusable OpenAI-compatible wire transports; not a plugin |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/runtime` | Provider registry, service selection, concurrency control, API routes, and settings UI |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/openai` | OpenAI-compatible language models, embeddings, TTS, file and live STT, and image generation |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/localai` | LocalAI language models, embeddings, reranking, TTS, file and live STT, and image generation |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/anthropic` | Language models through Anthropic's native Messages API |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/jina-cohere` | Reranking through Jina- and Cohere-compatible APIs |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/all` | Metadata-only DSH bundle containing the runtime and every provider maintained by this project |

See the individual provider guides for configuration and supported features:

- [OpenAI-compatible](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/openai)
- [LocalAI](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/localai)
- [Anthropic](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/anthropic)
- [Jina and Cohere](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/jina-cohere)

## Installation

Install the bundle into a DSH profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/all
```

The bundle installs the runtime and all vendor packages maintained by this project. Restart the profile, then configure connections, routes, and active services under **Settings → AI Providers**. Individual packages may also be installed separately for a custom deployment.

To use these language-model routes in place of DSH's stock routes, disable `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` and the stock `ui-settings-models` settings page in that profile. Keep DSH's core `llm` service enabled. For DSH Voice Input, keep its speech-to-text registry enabled but select the API-backed provider instead of the built-in SenseVoice provider.

This is an independent project maintained by Firefox2100. It is not an official DeepSeek Harness project and is not maintained or endorsed by the DSH maintainers.

## Development

Requires Node.js 22 or later and pnpm.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run test
pnpm run build
pnpm run release:check
```

See [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for branch and release policy.

## License

# @dsh-ai-providers/runtime

The shared provider runtime for DeepSeek Harness plugins.

It gives users one place to register reusable connections and DSH-managed credentials, select providers, and manage request concurrency. It exposes provider-neutral AI services to consumer plugins, so each plugin does not need its own vendor configuration and integration layer.

The runtime does not implement a vendor API, add an assistant, or make AI requests by itself. Install at least one vendor package and a plugin that consumes its services. More provider packages and capability contracts are planned for later releases.

## Install

Most users should install [`@dsh-ai-providers/all`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@dsh-ai-providers/all). For a custom deployment, install this runtime and only the desired provider plugins:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/runtime
```

[Documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/intro) · [Configuration](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/configuration) · [Source](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-ai-providers) · [Issues](https://github.com/Firefox2100/dsh-ai-providers/issues)

Licensed under GPL-3.0-only.

# DSH AI Providers

Reusable, provider-neutral AI services for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/DeepSeek-AI/DeepSeek-Harness).

DSH AI Providers is infrastructure for plugins that need AI capabilities beyond a single model backend. Users register a vendor connection and credential once, then reuse it for every capability that vendor supplies. Consumer plugins call stable services instead of implementing credentials, provider selection, concurrency control, and vendor APIs themselves.

It currently covers:

- language models;
- embeddings and reranking;
- text-to-speech and speech-to-text;
- image generation.

The project is primarily useful to plugin developers and to users of plugins built on it. Installing it alone does not add an assistant or start making AI requests: configure the providers you need, then install or build a plugin that consumes the services.

## Why use it

- Configure a connection and DSH-managed credential once instead of repeating secrets in every feature or plugin.
- Let users choose or change providers without coupling consumer plugins to vendor-specific APIs.
- Share capability contracts, live configuration, and concurrency limits across plugins.
- Retain vendor-specific controls where a common interface would otherwise hide useful behavior.

Additional vendor packages and services will be added as the ecosystem grows. The provider-neutral contracts are the foundation: existing consumer plugins should not need to be redesigned for every new backend.

## Documentation

- [Documentation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/intro)
- [简体中文文档](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/zh-Hans/docs/intro)
- [Installation](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/installation)
- [Configuration](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/getting-started/configuration)
- [Using services from another plugin](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/consumers/using-services)
- [Creating a provider package](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/providers/creating-provider)

## Packages

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/core` | Provider-neutral service contracts, errors, and shared types |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/openai-compatible` | Reusable OpenAI-compatible wire transports; not a plugin |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/runtime` | Provider registry, service selection, concurrency control, API routes, and settings UI |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/openai` | OpenAI-compatible language models, embeddings, TTS, file and live STT, and image generation |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/localai` | LocalAI language models, embeddings, reranking, TTS, file and live STT, and image generation |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/anthropic` | Language models through Anthropic's native Messages API |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/jina-cohere` | Reranking through Jina- and Cohere-compatible APIs |
| `@dsh-ai-providers/all` | Metadata-only DSH bundle containing the runtime and every provider maintained by this project |

See the individual provider guides for configuration and supported features:

- [OpenAI-compatible](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/openai)
- [LocalAI](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/localai)
- [Anthropic](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/anthropic)
- [Jina and Cohere](https://firefox2100.github.io/dsh-ai-providers/docs/official-providers/jina-cohere)

## Installation

Install the bundle into a DSH profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dsh-ai-providers/all
```

The bundle installs the runtime and all vendor packages maintained by this project. Restart the profile, then configure connections, routes, and active services under **Settings → AI Providers**. Individual packages may also be installed separately for a custom deployment.

To use these language-model routes in place of DSH's stock routes, disable `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` and the stock `ui-settings-models` settings page in that profile. Keep DSH's core `llm` service enabled. For DSH Voice Input, keep its speech-to-text registry enabled but select the API-backed provider instead of the built-in SenseVoice provider.

This is an independent project maintained by Firefox2100. It is not an official DeepSeek Harness project and is not maintained or endorsed by the DSH maintainers.

## Development

Requires Node.js 22 or later and pnpm.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run test
pnpm run build
pnpm run release:check
```

See [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for branch and release policy.

## License

[GPL-3.0-only](./LICENSE)

# 任务看板（dsh-task-board）

[English](README.en.md) | 中文

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@firetruck666/dsh-task-board)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@firetruck666/dsh-task-board)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node-%5E22.19.0%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24.0.0-339933)](README.md#环境要求)

DeepSeek Harness 的任务看板插件。它在 Web 界面的侧边栏加一个「任务看板」入口，用五列看板管理任务；任务交给 DSH 自己的会话真实执行，状态自动回写到卡片上。

插件不修改 DSH 源码，卸载后界面恢复原状。看板数据保存在 DSH 主进程（host）一侧，电脑和手机打开同一个部署看到的是同一块板，改动经 SSE 实时同步；窄屏自动进入紧凑布局。

## 目录

<!-- toc:start -->

- [环境要求](#环境要求)
- [安装](#安装)
- [更新](#更新)
- [主要能力](#主要能力)
- [数据保存在哪里](#数据保存在哪里)
- [从源码构建](#从源码构建)
- [贡献指南](#贡献指南)
- [常见问题](#常见问题)
- [命名约定](#命名约定)
- [许可证](#许可证)

<!-- toc:end -->

## 环境要求

- DeepSeek Harness `0.1.7-rc.2` 或更高。`0.1.7-rc.2` 是**最低支持版本**，不是「当前版本」：低于它的没验证过，**上限不设**——插件跟着 DSH 更新，升级 DSH 之后装最新版即可。加载失败时先按「常见问题」里的说明处理。
- Node.js `^22.19.0` 或 `>= 24.0.0`
- pnpm 10 或更高
- DSH 的 `web` profile

本插件只运行在 Web 图形界面上。

## 安装

三种方式，选一种。三条命令都在你自己的终端里执行。**桌面端（DSH 桌面应用）不用敲命令**：在它的「插件」页里添加同一个包名即可——那个 profile 由应用自己管理。

### 从 npm 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @firetruck666/dsh-task-board
```

适合日常使用。拿到的是最近一次正式发布的版本。

### 从 GitHub 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:FiretrUCK666/dsh-task-board
```

拿到的是仓库 `main` 分支的最新代码。它和 npm 装出来的一样是可直接使用的安装包，不是开发环境（没有测试、没有构建工具，改不了代码）。适合想第一时间用上还没发版改动的人；稳定性取决于仓库当时的状态。

### 本地开发安装

把仓库下载到本地后，在这个仓库目录里执行：

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm build
dsh plugin --profile web add .
```

这条路径用于改代码。详见下面的「从源码构建」。

本地安装是指向工作目录的链接（不是复制），所以挂载一次即可：改完代码只需 `pnpm build` 再重启 `dsh web`，不必重跑上面的安装命令。改 client 半区刷新页面即可，改 host 半区才需要重启——见「常见问题」里的「改了代码没生效」。

### 三种方式的区别

前两种是安装：拿到的都是可以直接使用的包，只包含发布清单里的文件（运行代码、源码、挂载声明、说明文档），差别只在版本新旧。第三种是开发：拿到的是完整仓库，能改代码、能运行测试。

| | 从 npm | 从 GitHub | 本地 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 用途 | 安装使用 | 安装使用 | 开发 |
| 拿到什么 | 最近一次发布版 | `main` 最新代码 | 你本地改动 |
| 版本特点 | 稳定 | 最新，可能不稳定 | 你自己决定 |
| 更新依据 | npm 上的版本号 | 仓库最新提交 | 安装的即本地目录，无需更新 |

### 安装之后

停掉正在运行的 `dsh web`，重新启动它，然后刷新页面。只刷新页面不够——插件的 host 半区在服务端进程里加载，必须重启才生效。重启后侧边栏就会出现「任务看板」入口。

入口和 DSH 自带的「插件」面板并排：点它，看板占用中间主区域；再点一次同一个入口、或点侧边栏里的任意会话，即可回到对话。

这个插件的开关在两处，各管各的：侧边栏「插件」→ 往下拉到「已安装」，那一行右边的开关是**总开关**；
或点开「任务看板」进它自己的页面，右上角那个开关做的是同一件事。**关掉 = 整个插件不加载**
（侧边栏入口、看板、清单、后台接口一起停）。页面里「包含的组件」下面还有四行，
每行一个开关，管各自那一半（看板 / 清单 / AI 接口）——详见「常见问题」。

### 不需要手动配置任何东西

装完就能用，不用改配置文件、不用手写任何声明。而且**不要去改 `cordis.patch.yml`**——插件那一行住在插件包里，安装命令只负责把这个包登记进 profile，两者一配合就装配好了；手工再补一行会造成同一个插件出现两条。

| 环节 | 谁做的 |
| --- | --- |
| 把插件登记进本机 profile | 安装命令（往 `dsh.profile.bundles` 加一个包名） |
| 插件那一行（id、包名） | 插件包里的 `cordis.patch.yml`，由 `package.json` 的 `dsh.bundle.patch` 指向，装配时自动生效 |
| 界面入口、看板舞台 | 插件自己注册到 DSH 的官方扩展点，启动时自动完成 |
| 数据存哪 | 自动使用 `~/.dsh/storages/dsh_task_board/` 目录，第一次运行时创建 |
| 插件显示的名字、说明、图标 | 包里的 `locale/` 与 `icon.svg`，DSH 直接读取 |
| 那个开关的位置 | 插件管理页的开关写 profile 里这一行的 `disabled`（关掉时才会写上） |

唯一必须你做的一步是**重启 `dsh web`**（host 半区在服务端进程里，不重启不会加载）。三种安装方式（npm、GitHub、本地）在这件事上完全一样。

这个插件没有设置项，也不需要设置面板：看板的行为（任务、定时、巡航、规则）全在看板界面上直接编辑，而开与关就是上面那个开关。

卸载：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove @firetruck666/dsh-task-board
```

同样需要重启 `dsh web`。卸载不会删除你的任务数据。

## 更新

看板 Header 右侧工具栏里有常驻的「检查更新」按钮，点一下即对比当前版本与最新版；有新版时它开一个「版本更新」对话框。

对话框里的「一键更新」知道自己该做什么，因为它读的是**你正在运行的那一份**的安装来源：安装方式与所属 profile 都从那一份所在的 profile 清单里读出来——所以同一台机器上 Web 端装的是本地开发、桌面端装的是 npm，两边各说各的，不会互相认错。

| 安装方式 | 「一键更新」做什么 |
| --- | --- |
| 从 npm 安装 | 按 npm 上的最新版本重装这一个包 |
| 从 GitHub 安装 | 按仓库 `main` 的当前提交重装 |
| 本地开发安装 | 在仓库目录里 `git pull --ff-only`，再按仓库自己声明的包管理器重建 `lib/` |
| 桌面端里装的 | 交给桌面端做（它的 profile 只能由它自己管理） |

更新完：能热载入的就地生效，需要重启的对话框会说明。**任务数据任何时候都不受影响。**

对话框里同时给出等价的终端命令，命令里的 profile 名就是你的那一份。命令也可以手动执行（把 `<profile>` 换成你自己的，一般是 `web`）：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @firetruck666/dsh-task-board@latest
```

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:FiretrUCK666/dsh-task-board
```

本地开发安装则是：

```sh
git pull --ff-only && pnpm run build
```

装了插件市场的话，也可以在它的「已安装」标签页里点「更新」。

**桌面端**：插件装在那个应用自己的 profile 里，而那个 profile 由应用托管——终端里的 `dsh plugin --profile desktop` 会被拒。在对话框里按「一键更新」，或在应用的「插件」页里重新添加，然后完全退出应用再打开。

## 主要能力

### 任务看板

- 五列：待规划 / 待办 / 进行中 / 待审核 / 已完成。卡片可以拖到别的列，同一列里也能上下拖，指定先后。
- 执行是真的：在详情里点「执行」，DSH 会话开始干活，跑完自动落到「待审核」。跑过几次、上次成没成，卡片上写着。
- AI 正在跑的卡有黄边，还没读过的有外环。
- 板顶一行数字：几个在等你、几张待审核。点它开通知中心。
- 通知中心收着所有等你处理的事；动态页按日分组，看最近发生了什么。
- 复核页是一次执行的完整记录，可以直接「通过 / 打回」。
- AI 在评论区里提问，当场就能答；**计划待审那张卡也一样**——「同意执行」直接作答，「要求修改」把它退回输入框，不必先去会话里走一趟。（哪台机器的宿主不提供就地作答时，那张卡会引用会话给的选项、说清为什么这里答不了，只留一扇「去会话回答」的门。）
- 每张卡的评论区就是它的 DSH 会话。排队发、插话发都行，图片和文件直接拖进去。
- 把侧栏里的会话或工作区拖到某一列，就得到一张绑好关系的卡。
- 定时跑、跑完接着跑、给某个会话按时间表发指令——两种自动化各管各的；发出去的指令可以带图片和文件，规则那一行会写明带了几个。
- 自动巡航：板头一颗开关，设好同时最多几件、哪些时段跑。
- 多选之后，改色、执行、删除一次做完。
- 详情能存成模板，新建时选一个就填好了；运行配置能存预设、设默认。
- 窄屏上列变成横向滑动，功能不少。

### 任务清单

- 按「＋新建一条」记一件事：**标题在最上面**，下面依次是正文、步骤、上下文备注（正文还可以拖进图片和文件）。左列写内容，右列定属性——优先级、状态、标签、三个日期、挂到哪张卡。挂到哪张卡有三个选择：**不挂**（先记下来，以后再说）、**挂到已有的卡**（那张卡里的内容一个字都不动）、**新建卡片**——选了新建，你会先看到**这张卡要用什么跑**（工作区 / Agent / 模型 / 思考程度 / 权限），它带着你看到的那一份出生，之后在卡上或这一行的详情里改。
- 清单是独立的，不必先变成卡片；挂上卡之后，它显示的状态就跟着那张卡在哪一栏走。
- 一行自己的状态是**五档**（待规划 / 待办 / 进行中 / 待审核 / 已完成），词与色都用看板那一套。没挂卡时五档随你选；挂着卡时跟着那张卡走，但**你自己按下的「已完成」压过卡片**——一件已经做完的事，不会因为卡还在跑就变回没做完。按那一枚状态芯片会跳到看板并打开它挂着的卡。
- **「问 AI」是这一页唯一交给 AI 的一按，没挂卡的条目也能按**：那张卡已经有对话就**接着说进那条对话**，还没有就**开一轮**——由卡自己决定，你不用挑。送过去的是这一条自己的内容（标题、标签、正文、步骤、备注，**以及正文带的图片与文件**），不是卡上的执行 Prompt，所以卡自己的 Prompt 是空的也照样问得出去。没挂卡的会先就地建一张卡，**卡就带着你眼前那一份运行配置出生**——所以配置不是按下去那一刻才冒出来问你的东西：详情右栏那块「运行配置」一直在，展开就是那五行（工作区 / Agent / 模型 / 思考程度 / 权限），点「改」就地换，按下去跑的就是屏上那一份。
- 看板那张卡片上有一枚「**挂 N 条 · 最急：X**」，按它跳到清单并**只看挂着这张卡的条目**（那是一枚筛选项，看得见也摘得掉）。
- 三个时间各自独立：开始、计划、截止——每个日期框的名字旁边都有一句注解（早于这天不动 / 想做完的那天 / 不能顺延的那天），展开详情里点开那一行时同样看得到。只有错过截止才变红，那一行写「超期 N 天」；计划滑了是黄的，写「落后 N 天」——承诺失守和计划推迟是两回事。
- 步骤打勾出进度条，优先级四档，标签随手打。
- 筛选全在左栏：日历、按日期（日期已过 / 日期未到 / 没定日期）、按多久没动（放着没动）、优先级、状态、日程、已删除。每一项都带数字，0 也写。
- 左栏顶上的日历能翻月、能回到今天，也能折成一行——翻月与回到今天是**同一个控件里的三格**（同一条边上的 `‹` / 回到今天 / `›`），「回到今天」没路可回时变灰、不消失。点某一天只看那天，搜索框下面会留下**一枚能按掉的日期芯片**——空列表也说得清是为什么空。
- 状态那一栏与看板是**同一套词、同一套颜色**：待规划 / 待办 / 进行中 / 待审核 / 已完成。行自己只存两个值（还没做、做完了），挂上卡之后跟着卡在哪一栏走；行首那颗珠子说这两个值，颜色说它在哪一栏。**那一枚状态芯片按得动**：按它就跳到看板、打开它挂着的那张卡。
- 标题、正文、备注、日期都在这一行里改，不另开窗口；**运行配置也在这一行里**（详情右栏那一块），而且它显示的正是**这一次要用的那一份**：挂着卡时是那张卡的（改的也是那张卡，与看板是同一处设置，不是第二份），还没挂卡时是「这一次要交给它的那一份」——那一块会说明它会跟着新卡走，之后在卡上改。
- **写正文和备注的框，高度是你自己的**：它不会随你打字自己长高，装不下就在框里滚；抓住**整条下沿**就能拉高拉低，拉完就记住（同一台设备上「新建一条」里那三个框也是这个高度）。下沿那条握痕一直画着，键盘也能用上下箭头拉。
- 正文可以带图片和文件：拖进去，或者点「＋」。它们随这一条保存，**变成卡片时一起过去**；行上有一枚回形针，写着这一条带了几个。
- **日期写错不会悄悄消失**：`@明天`、`10月15日`、`2026-10-15`、`10/15`、`Oct 15` 都认；**读不懂的三种情形各有各的说法**——写法不认识就教你再试一次（`2026-10-15`、`明天`、`周三`、`+3`），只写了日子没写年份而那天今年已过就让你把年份补上（猜一个等于把一天挪一年），日历上没有那一天（`2026-02-30`）就让你核对月份与日期。而你已经写下的日期一个字都不动。
- 日程页按天读，节名与行尾是同一套词：截止已过 / 计划已过 / 今天 / 明天 / 一周内 / 以后——「截止已过」说的是最后期限那天，「计划已过」说的是你打算做完的那天。一节有行才占一节；空的几天、以及没排进来的（已完成的、刚记下的）都在末尾那一行里带着数字说清楚。没写日期的进「没定日期」，开始日还没到的等在「还没开始」——**答不出「它为什么在这一页」的那几节各带一枚圆圈 i**（截止已过 / 计划已过 / 没定日期 / 还没开始），末尾那一行也带一枚；指着它或者按它，才会出现一句解释。按天的节（今天 / 明天 / 一周内 / 以后）不带——它的名字就是那一天。
- 删除有撤销；删掉的都在左栏底部「已删除」，30 天内能找回，也能彻底删除。
- 多选之后，改状态、设优先级、排在今天、问 AI、删除一次做完。
- 键盘：`A` 新建、`J`/`K` 移动、`X` 多选、`1`–`4` 优先级、`E` 改标题、`⌘Z` 撤销、`Esc` 一层一层收。

### 多台设备与 AI 入口

- 数据存在这台机器的 `~/.dsh/storages/dsh_task_board/`，人可读。换机器，拷这个目录就行。
- 手机上打开是同一份数据。断网也能用，连上后自动对齐。
- `/task` 把你写的话交给当前会话的模型；`/task-continue` 让它接着上次往下做。


## 数据保存在哪里

- 看板真相：`~/.dsh/storages/dsh_task_board/` 目录。`documents/` 下**每种数据一个文件**：`board.json` 是任务台账、巡航、定时预设、运行配置预设与删除墓碑；`items.json` 是任务清单。人可读、原子写入，可以直接整目录备份；删除这个目录等于清空看板与清单。
- 浏览器 localStorage 保存离线镜像和本地状态。两份**承载数据**的镜像是 `dsh.taskBoard.v1`（看板）与
  `dsh.taskBoard.items.v1`（任务清单）—— **两份都要备，只备一份等于清单那份丢了**。其余的键
  （`cruise` / `presets` / `runPresets` / `templates` / `drafts` / `preSync`）是这个浏览器自己的状态或
  一次性备份，不是另一份真相。**键名以 `src/client/` 里实际写下的为准**；这里列的是**哪些值得你
  操心**，不是全部键的清单。
- 第一次连接时如果本地数据与 host 有分歧，本地副本备份到 `dsh.taskBoard.preSync.v1`，host 为准。
- host 没有挂载存储后端时，看板自动退回纯 localStorage 模式。

## 从源码构建

前置：Node.js 22 或 24、pnpm、能访问官方 npm 源（类型和运行时 API 全部来自 `@deepseek-ai/*`，不需要 DSH 源码 checkout）。

```sh
git clone https://github.com/FiretrUCK666/dsh-task-board.git
cd dsh-task-board
pnpm install
pnpm build       # 产出 lib/index.js 和 lib/client.js
pnpm typecheck   # 类型检查
pnpm test        # 单元与契约测试
pnpm verify      # 独立插件静态门禁
```

`lib/` 是构建产物，但它随仓库一起提交。原因是从 GitHub 或 npm 安装时只会复制文件，不会执行构建，仓库里没有 `lib/` 的话装完就启动不了。改完源码要重新构建，并把 `lib/` 和源码放在同一次提交里（CI 会检查两者是否一致）。

仓库根目录的 `AGENTS.md` 记录了项目的约定、架构索引与发布流程，是 AI 助手在这个仓库里工作时用的依据。

## 贡献指南

欢迎提 Issue 与 Pull Request。动手前先读 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)：开发环境、提交 PR 前要跑的检查、硬性规范都在里面。报告加载失败类问题时，附上三个信息：DeepSeek Harness 版本、本插件版本、报错原文。

## 常见问题

**插件页面上的四个开关是什么。**
侧边栏「插件」→ 已安装 → 点「任务看板」→「包含的组件」列出四行，每行一个开关：

| 那一行 | 关掉之后 |
| --- | --- |
| 任务看板 | 侧栏面板列表里没有「任务看板」，看板面板不再出现 |
| 任务清单 | 侧栏面板列表里没有「任务清单」，清单面板不再出现 |
| **AI 接口** | **所有会话的 AI 都看不到本插件的工具、斜杠命令与系统提示**——它们从未被注册，不是被拒绝 |
| 任务看板（插件本体） | 整个插件不加载，上面三行随之无意义 |

「AI 接口」这一行是**装配层的开关**：关掉它，插件的那几个模块根本不加载，所以没有任何一次运行
时判断可以漏掉。清单与看板各自要开关，是因为它们是两个界面；而一个 npm 包只有一份浏览器产物，
所以这两行由宿主侧的模块宣告，浏览器开机时读一次。

**看板上的状态词都什么意思。**
它们读的是**同一份推导**，所以同一张卡在任何一处都是同一个答案：

| 你看到的词 | 它在说什么 | 什么时候消失 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **待你决断**（失败时写「失败待决断」） | 卡在「待审核」列，有跑完但那个**会话**你还没看过的结果 | 打开那个会话的评论区，或点「通过 / 打回」 |
| **等你处理 N 项** | N 个会话正挂起等你回答（审批 / 计划确认 / 提问） | **就在板内那张卡上回答**——同意执行、要求修改、或者选中它给的选项；不去会话也可以 |
| **待审核 M 张** | M 张卡在「待审核」列且那个会话你还没看过 | 同「待你决断」 |
| **新 N / 新留言** | 这张卡有还没看过的**新内容** | 点开卡片即消失 |
| **待处理 N** | N 个会话在等你（N > 1 时） | 逐个回答完 |
| **N 次执行** | 这张卡跑过几轮（历史，不是催你） | 不会自己消失 |
| **失败 · 已暂停** | 自动化因上次失败而暂停 | 在详情里重新启用 |

**「待你决断」和「新 N」是两件事**：「新」是「这张卡你没打开过」，「待你决断」是「那个会话你没
看过、也还没裁决」。**取消不算「待你决断」**——取消是中止，它只出现在评论线程和动态里。

**装完刷新页面看不到入口。**
host 半区在服务端进程里加载，必须重启 `dsh web`，只刷新页面不够。

**入口在哪、开关在哪。**
看板与清单是侧边栏里的两个面板图标，与 DSH 自带的「插件」面板并排。
这个插件的开关就在插件自己的页面上：侧边栏「插件」→ 已安装 → 点「任务看板」，
四行分别是看板、清单、AI 接口与宿主半区，每行一个开关，关掉哪行哪一半就不注册。
如果你看不到入口，说明这一端还在跑旧的前端资源——刷新页面即可。

**升级 DeepSeek Harness 之后插件加载失败（页面提示 Failed to load plugins）。**
DeepSeek Harness 的内部接口会随版本变化，本插件需要跟着改。先做这两步：

1. 把本插件更新到最新版，然后重启 `dsh web`：

   ```sh
   dsh plugin --profile web add @firetruck666/dsh-task-board@latest
   ```

2. 仍然失败，说明本插件还没跟上你用的那个 DSH 版本。请到 [Issues](https://github.com/FiretrUCK666/dsh-task-board/issues) 提交，附上三个信息：你的 DeepSeek Harness 版本、本插件版本（**在插件页的「已安装」列表里看——不是设置页，本插件没有设置项**）、页面上那段报错原文。有这三样就能直接定位。

**看板能打开，但多设备不同步、任务清单也一直是空的。**
这是 host 半区没加载成功的表现，也是升级 DSH 之后最容易被忽略的一种：看板本身仍在页面上正常工作，但数据只留在这一个浏览器里，另一台设备看到的不是同一块板，定时与巡航也不会真正触发。任务清单在这种情况下会明说「暂时读不到 host 上的清单，正在用本机的副本」，不会假装自己一条都没有。处理方式与上一条相同——更新插件、重启 `dsh web`。

**打开右侧栏之后看板变了样子。**
这是正常的响应式行为，不是故障。DSH 的右侧栏默认占视口约 45%、最少 300px，中栏硬保 400px，所以打开它之后**中间那块板本身变窄了**：看板的响应式看的是**自己盒子的宽度**（不是窗口宽度），板盒一旦窄过它的紧凑档阈值，五列就会变成横向滑动的列轨、并出现五等分的列导航标签。把右侧栏收回去就恢复。这条规则本意就是「板盒多宽就摆多宽」，侧栏开合、分屏、手机上都成立。

**改了代码没生效。**
改 host 半区（`src/index.ts`、`src/host/`）需要重启 `dsh web`；改 client 半区刷新页面即可。两种情况都要先 `pnpm build`。

**手机上打开位置不对，或反复开合侧栏会跳位。**
这是修复过的问题。如果仍然出现，先确认服务端进程是重启过的新版本：插件在板头会显示「服务端未重启 · 点此了解」，点开可以看到当前连接的服务端进程的启动时间。如果时间明显是旧的，说明这个地址连到了另一个没重启的实例。

**两端同时开着会不会重复执行定时任务。**
不会。定时、巡航、接续这类行为由 host 租约仲裁，同一时刻只有一个界面在执行，另一台设备切到前台后会接管并补上期间漏掉的状态。

**任务数据在哪，换电脑会丢吗。**
在 `~/.dsh/storages/dsh_task_board/` 目录。换电脑时把整个目录拷过去即可；浏览器里的 localStorage 只是离线镜像。

**找不到任务清单的入口。**
清单是**侧栏面板列表里紧跟「任务看板」的第二行**——把左栏展开就能看到两行图标，点第二行打开清单，
再点一下回到会话。侧栏收成一条窄图标带时，两行挨着排在一起。

如果那一行**根本没有**：多半是这一端还在跑旧的前端资源，**刷新页面**即可；还不行就去看插件页上
「任务清单」那个开关是不是被关了（见上面「四个开关」）。清单关掉不影响看板。

**切到看板面板时清单不见了。**
那不是坏了，是**主舞台一次只显示一个面板**——它本来就是这么设计的，不是两个能同屏的东西。
想回清单，点侧栏里清单那一行；想回对话，点「返回对话」或再点一次当前那一行。

**`dsh plugin` 报错找不到 pnpm。**
先安装 pnpm（`npm install -g pnpm`），再重新执行安装命令。

## 命名约定

| 用途 | 值 |
| --- | --- |
| 插件 id | `dsh-task-board` |
| npm 包名 | `@firetruck666/dsh-task-board` |
| 权限预设路由 | `/api/dsh-task-board/permissions` |
| 看板数据路由 | `/api/dsh-task-board/board`（含 `/items`、`/surfaces`、`/lease`、`/command`、`/events`） |
| 其余 host 路由 | `/api/dsh-task-board/session-state`、`/update`、`/client-report` |
| host 存储单元 | `dsh_task_board`（`documents/` 下每种数据一个文件） |
| 看板舞台 slot | `main`（`key: dsh-task-board`） |
| 任务清单舞台 slot | `main`（`key: dsh-task-board-items`，与看板同一个座位、不同键） |
| 侧栏入口 slot | `sidebar.panellist`（`id` 与各自的 `main` 键一致） |
| localStorage 键 | `dsh.taskBoard.v1` 等 |

插件 id 和包名是两件事：id 决定加载器行、浏览器资源路径、路由、存储单元和上面那几个扩展点；包名只是 pnpm 安装时的标识。包名带作用域不会改变 id。

本插件没有设置项，所以也没有设置路由和设置面板：插件市场里那条开关写的是 profile 行的 `disabled`（关掉时才写上），插件本身不声明任何设置字段。

## 许可证

MIT，见 LICENSE 文件。

# OMA for DeepSeek Harness Use project OMA skills and validation hooks in DeepSeek Harness (DSH). The plugin connects DSH tool execution and turn completion to the existing OMA CLI. It ships executable JavaScript and needs no build or install-time scripts. ## Requirements - DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2`, using Cordis `4.0.4`. - The OMA CLI on the host's PATH. Tested with OMA `15.0.17`. - An OMA project with `.agents/oma-config.yaml` or `.agents/oma-config.cue`. Initialize OMA through its normal project installation before enabling this plugin. The plugin does not install OMA or change your project configuration. DSH's filesystem skill provider discovers `.agents/skills//SKILL.md` directly, including the existing `resources/` and `_shared/` reference paths. ## Install With the DSH CLI installed, run from an OMA repository checkout: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add ./integrations/dsh --ignore-scripts dsh --profile web --dump-config dsh web ``` The configuration dump should contain the `dsh-plugin-oma` bundle and the `oma` plugin row. Choose your initialized OMA project as the DSH workspace. For Git installation, pin a commit containing this integration and select the subpackage using pnpm's Git source syntax: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add 'github:first-fluke/oh-my-agent#&path:/integrations/dsh' --ignore-scripts ``` Replace `` with the revision you reviewed. The package has no `prepare`, `build`, or post-install script. CLI profiles are distinct from the Desktop application's managed profile; these commands install into the CLI Web profile. To remove it: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-plugin-oma ``` ## Use Ask DSH to load an OMA skill, for example: ```text Load oma-qa and review the changes in this repository. ``` The skill supplies instructions. The plugin runs the project's configured OMA checks before and after tool calls and when a turn tries to finish. Hook output becomes DSH tool decisions or model-visible follow-up context. | DSH event | OMA event | Behavior | | --- | --- | --- | | `agent/created` | Direct runtime note | Explains the DSH runtime and project OMA skill location. | | `agent/created` | `oma state emit boundary` | Ties the active OMA session to the DSH session, for `oma state trajectory`. | | `tools/pre-execute` | `PreToolUse` | Denies a blocked call before its tool body runs; forwards approval requests and context. | | `tools/post-execute` | `PostToolUse` | Adds validation feedback to the next model request. | | `agent/turn-stopping` | `Stop` | Queues bounded follow-up work when an OMA check blocks completion. | The bridge invokes `oma hook run --vendor claude --event ` using an argument array, without a shell. Here `claude` selects OMA's hook JSON format. The DSH agent and session keep their existing identities. The bridge deliberately omits OMA `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit`: those handlers currently record host identity and contain Claude-specific prompt behavior. When an OMA session is active, a root agent records its DSH session id (and `DSH_HOME`, when set) on that session as a `boundary` event. `oma state trajectory` uses it to join the session's events with the DSH session log, so DSH turns, tool calls, and token usage appear in the trajectory. With no active OMA session there is nothing to attach to and nothing is recorded. Subagents are not recorded; their work lives in separate DSH sessions. DSH freezes tool arguments before its pre-execution hooks. If OMA requests a changed input, the plugin denies the call instead of executing the original input. The agent must make a new call with the required input. Post-execution feedback cannot undo a completed tool. Stop follow-up is bounded by `maxStopBlocks` to avoid an endless correction loop. Exhausting this bound does not establish that OMA validation passed; inspect the hook feedback and OMA result evidence. Automatic OMA keyword-triggered workflows and OMA native role dispatch are not part of this version. OMA Markdown workflows are instructions; they are not converted into DSH JavaScript workflow scripts. ## Configuration Override the `oma` row through your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: oma config: command: /absolute/path/to/oma commandArgs: [] timeoutMs: 10000 maxOutputBytes: 262144 maxInputBytes: 4194304 maxStopBlocks: 2 ``` `command` names one executable. `commandArgs` is a literal argument array, not a shell command. The host environment is inherited so OMA can use the project's configured tools. Hook processes run in the agent's actual working directory, including an explicit Bash `workdir`. Directories are resolved to their physical paths so symlinks and relative paths are checked from the same location as the tool. Cancellation, agent disposal, and plugin unload terminate owned hook processes. A project without an OMA marker is left alone. In an initialized project, a failed, timed-out, or malformed pre-tool hook denies that call. A post-tool failure becomes feedback, and a stop-hook failure uses the same bounded follow-up mechanism. ## Verify From the OMA repository root: ```sh bun run test:dsh ``` The tests cover the shipped bridge and subprocess runner. The release verification also uses published DSH packages for skill discovery, tool execution, and agent continuation. Its model responses are deterministic test fixtures; it makes no paid model calls. Verified on macOS with DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`, Cordis `4.0.4`, and OMA `15.0.17`: 19 tests pass, all 33 project OMA skills are discovered, and the real OMA CLI blocks a guarded tool call while allowing a benign call. ## References - [DSH skill discovery](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/reference/subsystems/skills) - [DSH plugin packaging](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/develop/basic/publish) - [DSH tool events](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/reference/subsystems/tools) - [pnpm Git subdirectory sources](https://pnpm.io/package-sources#install-from-a-git-repository-combining-different-parameters) # oh-my-agent: The Multi-Agent Harness That Checks the Work [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/oh-my-agent?color=cb3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/oh-my-agent) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/oh-my-agent?color=cb3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/oh-my-agent) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/first-fluke/oh-my-agent?style=flat&logo=github)](https://github.com/first-fluke/oh-my-agent) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/first-fluke/oh-my-agent)](https://github.com/first-fluke/oh-my-agent/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Last Updated](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/first-fluke/oh-my-agent?label=updated&logo=git)](https://github.com/first-fluke/oh-my-agent/commits/main) [한국어](./docs/README.ko.md) | [中文](./docs/README.zh.md) | [Português](./docs/README.pt.md) | [日本語](./docs/README.ja.md) | [Français](./docs/README.fr.md) | [Español](./docs/README.es.md) | [Nederlands](./docs/README.nl.md) | [Polski](./docs/README.pl.md) | [Русский](./docs/README.ru.md) | [Deutsch](./docs/README.de.md) | [Tiếng Việt](./docs/README.vi.md) | [ภาษาไทย](./docs/README.th.md) **Agents narrate success. oh-my-agent checks the artifacts.** Spawning parallel agents is the easy part. The hard part is knowing whether they actually did the work. "Tests pass, all criteria met" costs an agent nothing to say, and nothing inside that same session can contradict it. oh-my-agent makes the claim falsifiable. A Stop hook refuses to end your session until your project's own `typecheck` / `test` / `lint` script exits 0. A gate command decides whether a workflow really ran by looking for the artifacts it must have left behind — and its JSON verdict, not the agent's summary, is the result. In `/ralph`, the workflow prompt dispatches a judge, briefed on the criteria only, that re-verifies every criterion each round, including the ones that already passed. Gate decisions are appended to a per-session event log that you can read afterwards with `oma state`. Then it runs that same discipline across a dozen agent runtimes from one portable `.agents/` directory. Follow [Quick Start](./web/docs/getting-started/quick-start.md) to choose a skill preset, run `oma doctor`, and ask a named skill for one scoped change. Record the file, check command, and exit status. ![oh-my-agent explainer](./docs/assets/video/oh-my-agent-explainer.gif) [Watch the full video (35s)](./docs/assets/video/oh-my-agent-explainer.mp4) ## Quick Start Run the OMA installer and choose a skill preset for your project. The install scripts auto-install bun, uv, and serena if they're missing. ```bash # macOS / Linux — auto-installs bun, uv & serena if missing curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/first-fluke/oh-my-agent/main/cli/install.sh | bash ``` ```powershell # Windows (PowerShell) — auto-installs bun, uv & serena if missing irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/first-fluke/oh-my-agent/main/cli/install.ps1 | iex ``` ```bash # Or manual (any OS, requires bun + uv + serena) bunx oh-my-agent@latest ``` Pick a preset and you're ready: | Preset | What You Get | |--------|-------------| | **All** | **Every agent and skill** | | Backend | architecture + backend + brainstorm + db + debug + dev-workflow + pm + qa + scm | | Content | academic-writer + design + image + scm + translator + voice | | DevOps | architecture + brainstorm + debug + dev-workflow + observability + pm + qa + scm + tf-infra | | Frontend | architecture + brainstorm + debug + design + frontend + pm + qa + scm | | Fullstack | architecture + backend + brainstorm + db + debug + design + dev-workflow + frontend + mobile + pm + qa + scm + tf-infra | | Fullstack Mobile | architecture + backend + brainstorm + db + debug + design + dev-workflow + mobile + pm + qa + scm | | Fullstack Web | architecture + backend + brainstorm + db + debug + design + dev-workflow + frontend + pm + qa + scm | | Mobile | architecture + brainstorm + debug + mobile + pm + qa + scm | | Research | academic-writer + hwp + market + pdf + scholar + scm + search + translator | ## Agent Integrations `oh-my-agent` uses `.agents/` as the shared source for agent skills, workflows, rules, and verification gates.
